project.name: Medical View
project.description: MediView is a medical imaging and diagnosis platform built around a single Study lifecycle (todo -> in-progress -> re-diagnosis -> done). Patients self-register, book a doctor within the doctor's working hours, and their x-ray images are imported into the Study (simulated by an admin, since there is no physical modality). A doctor opens the Study in a Cornerstone.js DICOM Viewport under a single-writer lock, diagnoses, exports the result and prescription, and marks the Study done or re-diagnosis. Patients then pay the bill from an in-app wallet. Admins are seeded, onboard doctors after verifying credentials, and hold audited break-glass permissions. Auth, DICOM import, and Payment each sit behind a feature flag so the platform runs fully in-house now and can adopt external providers later. Built as .NET 10 microservices with Domain-Driven Design + Clean Architecture, deployed on Azure.

techStack.architecture: Domain-Driven Design + Clean Architecture (Domain / Application / Infrastructure / Api) + Microservices + Repository + Unit of Work + SOLID
techStack.database: PostgreSQL - one schema per bounded context, FKs only inside a schema, cross-service references by uuid
techStack.messaging: MassTransit over RabbitMQ (local) / Azure Service Bus (prod), Transactional Outbox
techStack.cloud: Azure (Container Apps, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Cache for Redis, Service Bus, Key Vault, ACR, Blob Storage, Application Insights)
techStack.auth: JWT access tokens + rotating refresh tokens
techStack.serviceComms: gRPC (sync queries) + MassTransit/RabbitMQ with transactional outbox (async events)
techStack.dataAccess: EF Core for writes, Dapper for read models/reports

sections.name: Foundation & Solution Structure
sections.goal: A compiling, conventioned monorepo with .NET 10 SDK, central package management, and Clean Architecture conventions agreed.

tasks.title: Install and verify .NET 10 SDK
tasks.details: Install the .NET 10 SDK on all dev machines/CI. Verify with `dotnet --list-sdks` and `dotnet --version` (expect 10.x).
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet --version` reports a 10.x SDK
steps: Download the .NET 10 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download and run the installer.
Open a NEW terminal (the PATH only updates in fresh shells).
Run `dotnet --version` and confirm it prints 10.x.
Run `dotnet --list-sdks` to check no older SDK shadows it.
Create `global.json` at the repo root: `dotnet new globaljson --sdk-version 10.0.100 --roll-forward latestFeature`.
Commit `global.json` so every machine and CI runner pins the same SDK.

tasks.title: Initialize git repository and .gitignore
tasks.details: Create the repo, run `dotnet new gitignore`, add README, LICENSE, and a CONTRIBUTING doc. Adopt trunk-based or GitFlow branching and document it.
acceptanceCriteria: Repo initialized with dotnet .gitignore and README committed
steps: Create the project folder: `mkdir MediView && cd MediView`.
Run `git init` and set the default branch: `git branch -M main`.
Generate the ignore file: `dotnet new gitignore` (covers bin/, obj/, .vs/, user secrets).
Append these lines to `.gitignore`: `appsettings.*.local.json`, `.env`, `*.user`, `/artifacts/`.
Add a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` so line endings stay stable across OSes.
Create `README.md` with a one-paragraph project description and the run command.
Commit: `git add . && git commit -m "chore: init repository"`.
Create the remote on GitHub and push: `git remote add origin <url> && git push -u origin main`.

tasks.title: Create solution and top-level folders
tasks.details: Run `dotnet new sln -n MedicalView`. Create `src/`, `tests/`, `build/`, `deploy/`, `docs/` folders. Add solution folders per bounded context.
acceptanceCriteria: MedicalView.sln builds with `dotnet build` (empty)
steps: From the repo root run `dotnet new sln -n MediView`.
Create the folder skeleton: `mkdir -p src/BuildingBlocks src/Services src/Gateway src/Web docs build`.
Add `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/adr/` (one file per architecture decision).
Add `build/` for Dockerfiles and CI scripts.
Commit the empty structure so the layout is reviewable before any code exists.
Confirm `dotnet sln list` runs cleanly (it will report no projects yet).

tasks.title: Enable Central Package Management
tasks.details: Add `Directory.Packages.props` (CPM, `ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true`) and `Directory.Build.props` (nullable enable, LangVersion latest, ImplicitUsings, TreatWarningsAsErrors).
acceptanceCriteria: All projects resolve versions from Directory.Packages.props
steps: Create `Directory.Packages.props` at the repo root.
Inside `<Project>`, add `<PropertyGroup><ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally></PropertyGroup>`.
Add an `<ItemGroup>` with `<PackageVersion Include="..." Version="..." />` for each dependency.
Seed it with: Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL, MediatR, FluentValidation, MassTransit, StackExchange.Redis, Serilog.AspNetCore, Dapper.
In every .csproj, reference packages WITHOUT a Version attribute: `<PackageReference Include="MediatR" />`.

Create `Directory.Build.props` with shared settings: `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`, `<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>`, `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`, `<LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>`.
Run `dotnet restore` and fix any version that is now declared in two places.

tasks.title: Add .editorconfig and analyzers
tasks.details: Add `.editorconfig` with team code style, enable Roslyn analyzers and (optionally) StyleCop.Analyzers via CPM.
acceptanceCriteria: Style violations surface as build warnings/errors
steps: Run `dotnet new editorconfig` at the repo root.
Set indentation and C# style rules: `csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped:warning`.
Turn key analyzer rules into errors, e.g. `dotnet_diagnostic.CA2007.severity = none` (no ConfigureAwait noise in ASP.NET) and `dotnet_diagnostic.CA1062.severity = warning`.
In `Directory.Build.props` add `<EnableNETAnalyzers>true</EnableNETAnalyzers>` and `<AnalysisLevel>latest-recommended</AnalysisLevel>`.
Verify formatting: `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` (this becomes a CI gate later).
Commit `.editorconfig` before writing code so no file is ever reformatted wholesale later.

tasks.title: Create dotnet tool manifest
tasks.details: Run `dotnet new tool-manifest` and `dotnet tool install dotnet-ef` so EF Core CLI is pinned per-repo.
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet ef --version` works via local tool manifest
steps: Run `dotnet new tool-manifest` (creates `.config/dotnet-tools.json`).
Install EF tooling locally: `dotnet tool install dotnet-ef`.
Install the format tool if needed: `dotnet tool install dotnet-format`.
Commit `.config/dotnet-tools.json`.
On any new machine, run `dotnet tool restore` to get identical tool versions.
Confirm with `dotnet ef --version`.

tasks.title: Document DDD + Clean Architecture layering
tasks.details: Write docs/architecture.md defining Domain-Driven Design on top of Clean Architecture. Four concentric layers per service: (1) Domain = entities, aggregates, value objects, domain events, domain services and repository interfaces (Enterprise Business Rules); (2) Application = use cases as commands/queries/handlers, DTOs, validators (Application Business Rules); (3) Infrastructure = EF Core, Redis, message bus, blob and external gateways (Interface Adapters); (4) Api/Web = ASP.NET Core or Blazor host and DI composition root (Frameworks & Drivers). The dependency rule is absolute: source dependencies point inward only.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/architecture.md shows the four DDD / Clean Architecture layers and the inward-only dependency rule
steps: Create `docs/architecture.md`.

Write the four layers as a table: Domain (entities, aggregates, VOs, domain events, repository INTERFACES), Application (use cases, DTOs, validators, port interfaces), Infrastructure (EF Core, Redis, bus, blob, gRPC clients), Api (endpoints, middleware, DI composition root).
State the dependency rule explicitly: Api -> Infrastructure -> Application -> Domain, and Domain references nothing.
Map the layers to Clean Architecture's rings: Domain = Enterprise Business Rules, Application = Application Business Rules, Infrastructure = Interface Adapters, Api = Frameworks & Drivers.
Add the rule of thumb: if a class needs a framework type, it does not belong in Domain — put an interface in Domain and the implementation in Infrastructure.
Embed the architecture diagram image and commit.

tasks.title: Define the per-microservice project template (separate projects per layer)
tasks.details: Standardize every microservice as four SEPARATE projects, matching the reference solution layout: `MediView.<Service>.Domain` (classlib), `MediView.<Service>.Application` (classlib), `MediView.<Service>.Infrastructure` (classlib) and `MediView.<Service>.Api` (webapi startup project). Blazor host projects use the `.Web` suffix. Wire references inward only: Api -> Infrastructure -> Application -> Domain, and Application references Domain only. Commands: `dotnet new classlib -n MediView.<Service>.Domain`, `... .Application`, `... .Infrastructure`, `dotnet new webapi -n MediView.<Service>.Api`, then `dotnet sln add` and `dotnet add reference` to connect the layers.
acceptanceCriteria: A sample service exists as four projects with references pointing inward only
steps: Pick the first service to template — use `Patient`.
Create the folder: `mkdir -p src/Services/Patient && cd src/Services/Patient`.

Create the four projects: `dotnet new classlib -n MediView.Patient.Domain`, `... -n MediView.Patient.Application`, `... -n MediView.Patient.Infrastructure`, then `dotnet new webapi -n MediView.Patient.Api`.
Delete the auto-generated `Class1.cs` from each classlib.
Wire references INWARD ONLY: `dotnet add MediView.Patient.Application reference MediView.Patient.Domain`.
Then `dotnet add MediView.Patient.Infrastructure reference MediView.Patient.Application`.
Then `dotnet add MediView.Patient.Api reference MediView.Patient.Infrastructure`.
Add all four to the solution: `dotnet sln ../../../MediView.sln add **/*.csproj`.
Build to confirm: `dotnet build`.
Verify the rule by trying to add a reference from Domain to Infrastructure — then remove it; that direction must never be committed.

tasks.title: Create a reusable service scaffold
tasks.details: Package the four-project layout as a `dotnet new` template (or a pwsh/bash generator) so every new microservice is created identically with the Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects, base references, and analyzers already wired.
acceptanceCriteria: Running the scaffold produces a ready-to-build Clean Architecture service
steps: Copy the four Patient projects into a template folder: `build/templates/service/`.
Replace every occurrence of `Patient` with the token `ServiceName` in file names and namespaces.
Add `.template.config/template.json` declaring `sourceName: ServiceName` and a short name like `mediview-service`.
Install it locally: `dotnet new install ./build/templates/service`.
Test it: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Booking -o src/Services/Booking`.
Confirm the generated projects build and their references still point inward.
Document the command in `README.md` so every new service is created the same way.

tasks.title: Enforce the dependency rule in the build
tasks.details: Keep MediView.<Svc>.Domain free of every non-BCL package reference (no EF Core, no ASP.NET). Add an architecture guard so a Domain project that references Infrastructure fails the build. Folders are named after domain concepts (Studies/, Patients/), never after patterns (Repositories/).
acceptanceCriteria: A Domain project referencing Infrastructure or EF Core fails the build
steps: Open `MediView.<Svc>.Domain.csproj` and confirm it contains NO `<PackageReference>` beyond the BCL.
Create a test project: `dotnet new xunit -n MediView.ArchitectureTests -o tests/MediView.ArchitectureTests`.
Add the guard package: `dotnet add package NetArchTest.Rules`.

Write a test asserting Domain does not depend on Infrastructure: `Types.InAssembly(domainAssembly).ShouldNot().HaveDependencyOn("MediView.Patient.Infrastructure").GetResult().IsSuccessful` must be true.
Add a second test: Domain must not depend on `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`.
Add a third: Application must not depend on Infrastructure.
Run `dotnet test` and watch it pass.
Deliberately add a bad reference, re-run, and confirm the test FAILS — an unverified guard is not a guard.
Wire `dotnet test` into CI so the rule is enforced on every PR.

tasks.title: Define aggregate boundaries
tasks.details: Document one transaction = one aggregate. Roots: Study (status, history, lock), Report (addenda), Prescription (items), Bill (items, payments), Wallet (transactions), Appointment, Doctor (credentials). Cross-aggregate consistency is eventual, via domain/integration events.
acceptanceCriteria: Every entity belongs to exactly one documented aggregate
steps: Create `docs/aggregates.md`.

List each aggregate root and the entities inside it: Study (status, status history, lock), Report (addenda), Prescription (items), Bill (items, payments), Wallet (transactions), Appointment, Doctor (credentials).
For each, write the invariant it protects, e.g. 'a Study's status only changes through an allowed transition'.
Write the rule: one transaction modifies exactly ONE aggregate.
State that cross-aggregate changes happen through domain events, so consistency between aggregates is eventual.
Note that aggregates reference each other BY ID only, never by object reference.
Review the list against the DBML table groups and fix any table that has no owning aggregate.

sections.name: Shared Kernel & Building Blocks
sections.goal: Reusable building blocks (base entities, Result type, generic repository + Unit of Work, domain events, error handling, integration-event contracts) that every service consumes.

tasks.title: Create BuildingBlocks.Domain library
tasks.details: Create BuildingBlocks.Domain: Entity / AuditableEntity, AggregateRoot, ValueObject, IDomainEvent, DomainService marker, and strongly-typed ids - the DDD tactical building blocks every aggregate is composed from.
acceptanceCriteria: Domain primitives compile and are unit-testable
steps: Create the project: `dotnet new classlib -n MediView.BuildingBlocks.Domain -o src/BuildingBlocks/MediView.BuildingBlocks.Domain`.
Add it to the solution and confirm it has zero package references.
Add `Entity.cs`: an abstract class with `public Guid Id { get; protected set; }` and equality by Id.

Add `AggregateRoot.cs` inheriting Entity, holding `private readonly List<IDomainEvent> _domainEvents` exposed as `IReadOnlyCollection<IDomainEvent>`, plus `RaiseDomainEvent()` and `ClearDomainEvents()`.
Add `ValueObject.cs`: abstract class with `GetEqualityComponents()` and equality/hashcode built from it.
Add `IDomainEvent.cs` as a marker interface (`: INotification` once MediatR is wired).
Add `AuditableEntity.cs` with `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt` (set by the DbContext interceptor, not by hand).
Add `DomainException.cs` for invariant violations.
Build and commit.

tasks.title: Implement Result and Error types
tasks.details: Add a Result / Result<T> and Error record for railway-style flow (avoid exceptions for expected failures). Include common error factories (NotFound, Conflict, Validation).
acceptanceCriteria: Result<T> supports success/failure with typed errors; unit tested
steps: In BuildingBlocks.Domain (or a new `.Application`), add `Error.cs` as a record: `record Error(string Code, string Message)` with a static `None`.
Add `Result.cs`: `IsSuccess`, `IsFailure`, `Error`, private constructor guarding that a success cannot carry an error.
Add static factories: `Result.Success()`, `Result.Failure(Error)`.
Add `Result<T>` with a `Value` property that THROWS if accessed on a failure — this is what stops silent bugs.
Add implicit conversion from `T` to `Result<T>` so handlers can `return study;`.
Create `DomainErrors.cs` with grouped static errors, e.g. `DomainErrors.Study.AlreadyLocked`.
Write a quick unit test asserting `Result.Failure(...).Value` throws.

tasks.title: Define repository and Unit of Work abstractions
tasks.details: In BuildingBlocks.Application define IRepository<T>, IReadRepository<T>, ISpecification<T>, and IUnitOfWork. Depend on abstractions only (DIP).
acceptanceCriteria: Abstractions defined with no infrastructure dependency
steps: In BuildingBlocks.Domain add `IRepository<T>` where `T : AggregateRoot` with `GetByIdAsync`, `Add`, `Update`, `Remove`.
Keep every method returning domain types only — no `IQueryable`, no EF types leak here.
Add `IUnitOfWork` with a single `Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken)`.
Write the rule in a code comment: aggregate-specific repository interfaces (e.g. `IStudyRepository`) live in the Domain folder of THEIR aggregate, not in a shared Repositories folder.
Decide and document: `SaveChangesAsync` IS the Unit of Work — do not wrap DbContext in a class that only forwards.
Build; nothing should reference EF Core yet.

tasks.title: Implement EF Core generic repository + UoW
tasks.details: Create BuildingBlocks.Infrastructure with EfRepository<T>, specification evaluator, and EfUnitOfWork wrapping DbContext.SaveChanges. Keep provider-agnostic.
acceptanceCriteria: Generic repo + UoW pass integration tests against a DbContext
steps: Create `dotnet new classlib -n MediView.BuildingBlocks.Infrastructure -o src/BuildingBlocks/MediView.BuildingBlocks.Infrastructure`.
Reference BuildingBlocks.Domain and add `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL`.
Add `Repository<T>` implementing `IRepository<T>` over `DbContext`, using `DbSet<T>` for reads by id.
Implement `GetByIdAsync` with `FindAsync` (uses the identity map, avoiding a round trip when already tracked).
Make `DbContext` implement `IUnitOfWork` so `SaveChangesAsync` satisfies the interface directly.
Add an `AuditableEntityInterceptor : SaveChangesInterceptor` setting `CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt` from `IClock`.
Add a `DomainEventsInterceptor` that collects events from tracked aggregates after save.
Register both interceptors in `AddInfrastructure()`.
Build and commit.

tasks.title: Add domain event dispatch via MediatR
tasks.details: Register MediatR; dispatch IDomainEvent from SaveChanges interceptor after commit. Provide INotificationHandler base.
acceptanceCriteria: Domain events raised on an aggregate are handled after persistence
steps: Add the MediatR package to BuildingBlocks.Application.
Make `IDomainEvent` inherit `MediatR.INotification`.
In the `DomainEventsInterceptor`, override `SavedChangesAsync` so events publish only AFTER the transaction commits.
Collect events: iterate `ChangeTracker.Entries<AggregateRoot>()`, take their events, then call `ClearDomainEvents()` BEFORE publishing (or you will loop).
Publish each event with `IPublisher.Publish(domainEvent, ct)`.
Create a sample handler `class StudyStatusChangedHandler : INotificationHandler<StudyStatusChanged>` and log the event.
Test: change a Study's status, save, and confirm the handler runs exactly once.
Document the distinction: DOMAIN events stay in-process; INTEGRATION events cross services via the bus.

tasks.title: Global exception handling + ProblemDetails
tasks.details: Add exception-handling middleware mapping exceptions/Result errors to RFC7807 ProblemDetails with correlation id.
acceptanceCriteria: Unhandled/handled errors return consistent ProblemDetails JSON
steps: In BuildingBlocks.Infrastructure add `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs` implementing `IMiddleware`.
Wrap `await next(context)` in try/catch.

Map exception types to status codes: `DomainException` -> 400, `NotFoundException` -> 404, `StudyLockedException` -> 409, `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` -> 409, `ValidationException` -> 400 with the error dictionary, everything else -> 500.
Build a `ProblemDetails` (RFC 7807) response with `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, and the correlation id in `extensions`.
Never leak stack traces in Production — include them only when `IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment()`.
Log 500s at Error with the correlation id; log 4xx at Information (they are client mistakes, not incidents).
Register it: `app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>()` as the FIRST middleware.
Test by throwing each exception type from a scratch endpoint and checking the status codes.

tasks.title: Add validation pipeline (FluentValidation)
tasks.details: Add FluentValidation + a MediatR validation behavior so command/query inputs validate before handlers run.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid commands short-circuit with 400 + validation errors
steps: Add FluentValidation and FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions to BuildingBlocks.Application.
Create `ValidationBehaviour<TRequest,TResponse> : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest,TResponse>`.
In `Handle`, resolve `IEnumerable<IValidator<TRequest>>`; if none, call `next()` immediately.
Run all validators, collect failures, and if any exist throw `ValidationException` (or return a failed `Result`).
Register the behaviour: `cfg.AddOpenBehavior(typeof(ValidationBehaviour<,>))` in the MediatR registration.
Register validators by assembly scan: `services.AddValidatorsFromAssembly(assembly)`.
Write one validator, e.g. `BookAppointmentCommandValidator` requiring a future `ScheduledStart`.
Verify an invalid command returns 400 with field errors and never reaches the handler.

tasks.title: Create Contracts library for integration events
tasks.details: Separate BuildingBlocks.Contracts package holding versioned integration-event records (UserRegistered, StudyLocked, ReportFinalized, PrescriptionIssued, BillPaid, FollowUpScheduled).
acceptanceCriteria: Contracts package referenced by publishers and consumers only
steps: Create the project: `dotnet new classlib -n MediView.Contracts -o src/BuildingBlocks/MediView.Contracts`.
Keep it dependency-free (records only) so any service can reference it without pulling in a stack.
Create one folder per publishing service: `Auth/`, `Patient/`, `Reporting/`, `Prescription/`, `Billing/`, `Booking/`.
Define the events as records with an interface marker: `public record UserRegistered(Guid UserId, string Email, DateTimeOffset OccurredOn) : IIntegrationEvent;`.
Add the rest: `StudyLocked`, `StudyStatusChanged`, `ReportFinalized`, `PrescriptionIssued`, `BillPaid`, `FollowUpScheduled`.
Give every event `Guid EventId` and `DateTimeOffset OccurredOn` — consumers need them for idempotency and ordering.
Version by namespace, e.g. `MediView.Contracts.Reporting.V1`; when a shape must change, add `V2` and keep V1 until every consumer migrates.
Write the rule in the project README: NEVER change or repurpose a field on a published event — only add optional fields.
Reference `MediView.Contracts` from publishers and consumers ONLY (Api/Infrastructure), never from a Domain project.
Add an architecture test asserting no Domain project references MediView.Contracts.

tasks.title: Add pagination and query result envelopes
tasks.details: Provide PagedResult<T>, paging request DTOs, and sorting helpers reused across query endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: Paged endpoints share a single PagedResult<T> shape
steps: In BuildingBlocks.Application add `PagedResult<T>` with `Items`, `TotalCount`, `Page`, `PageSize`, `HasNextPage`.
Add a `PagedQuery` base with `Page` and `PageSize`, defaulting PageSize to 20 and clamping it to a max of 100.
Add an `IQueryable<T>.ToPagedResultAsync(page, size, ct)` extension that runs `CountAsync` then `Skip/Take`.
Add a cursor-based variant for the worklist: `CursorResult<T>` with `NextCursor`, because offset paging drifts as rows are inserted.
Forbid in-memory paging in review: never `.ToList().Skip(...)`.
Return the envelope from list endpoints so the UI can render page counts.

tasks.title: Establish EF Core conventions
tasks.details: Define the EF Core conventions every service follows: one DbContext per bounded context on Npgsql; an IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> per aggregate; value objects mapped as owned types; optimistic concurrency via the Postgres xmin token; connection resiliency with EnableRetryOnFailure; reads use AsNoTracking with projections; lazy loading disabled; and MassTransit EF Outbox tables. Migrations live in the Infrastructure project (`dotnet ef migrations add`, `dotnet ef database update`).
acceptanceCriteria: A documented EF Core convention set is applied by the shared repository/UoW
steps: Create `docs/efcore-conventions.md` and add these rules as a checklist.
One DbContext per service; call `modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema("patient")` in `OnModelCreating`.
One `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` per aggregate in `Persistence/Configurations/`; apply with `ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly`.
Map value objects with `OwnsOne`; map enums with `.HasConversion<string>()` so the database stores readable values.
Add optimistic concurrency: `b.Property(x => x.Version).IsRowVersion()` mapped to Postgres `xmin`.
Configure Npgsql with `EnableRetryOnFailure()` and `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()`.
Disable lazy loading; require explicit `Include` or projection.
Use `AsNoTracking()` plus `Select` into a DTO for every read query.
Add the MassTransit EF outbox tables to the DbContext.
Add a rule: no `DbSet` for another service's tables, ever.

tasks.title: Adopt the reviewed schema baseline (schema per service, FKs only inside a schema)
tasks.details: Take db-v2.sql as the target data model. Rule: one PostgreSQL schema per bounded context (auth, identity, patient, booking, imaging, reporting, prescription, billing, notification, audit) with foreign keys ONLY inside a schema; a reference to another service's data is a plain uuid column documented as a cross-service reference. Conventions: uuid primary keys defaulting to gen_random_uuid(), snake_case names, created_at/updated_at as timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), CHECK constraints for every status column, UNIQUE on all join tables, and an index on every FK/lookup column.
acceptanceCriteria: Every service's EF model follows the schema baseline and no FK crosses a service boundary
steps: Open `mediview.dbml` and treat it as the target model.
Create the schemas per bounded context: auth, identity, patient, booking, imaging, reporting, prescription, billing, notification, config, audit.
Adopt the boundary rule: foreign keys ONLY inside a schema.
For a cross-service reference, use a plain `uuid` column with an XML comment naming the owning service — no FK.
Apply the conventions: uuid PKs defaulting to `gen_random_uuid()`, snake_case, `timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`.
Add a CHECK constraint (or enum conversion) for every status column.
Add a UNIQUE constraint on every join table's natural key pair.
Add an index on every FK and every column used in a WHERE or ORDER BY.
Add an architecture test or migration review step confirming no FK crosses a schema.

tasks.title: Result type and pipeline behaviours
tasks.details: Add Result<T> with error codes for expected failures (exceptions only for the exceptional), plus MediatR-style pipeline behaviours for validation (FluentValidation), logging, and transactions so handlers hold domain logic only.
acceptanceCriteria: Handlers contain no try/catch plumbing; validation runs in the pipeline
steps: Create `LoggingBehaviour<TRequest,TResponse>` logging the request name, correlation id and elapsed ms.
Create `TransactionBehaviour<TRequest,TResponse>` that opens a transaction only for `ICommand` requests, commits on success, rolls back on exception.
Skip the transaction for `IQuery` requests — a read does not need one.
Register behaviours in order: Logging -> Validation -> Transaction -> handler (order matters; validation must run before the transaction opens).
Refactor one handler to remove its try/catch and rely on the pipeline.
Confirm a thrown exception mid-handler leaves no partial write in the database.

tasks.title: Inject the clock, standardise money and time
tasks.details: Add IClock (never DateTime.Now); use DateTimeOffset.UtcNow everywhere and store timestamptz. Money is decimal with an explicit currency, never double.
acceptanceCriteria: No direct DateTime.Now/UtcNow calls outside the clock implementation
steps: Add `IClock` with `DateTimeOffset UtcNow` to BuildingBlocks.Domain.
Add `SystemClock : IClock` in Infrastructure returning `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`.
Register it as a singleton.
Replace every `DateTime.Now` / `DateTime.UtcNow` in the codebase with the injected clock.
Add an analyzer rule or architecture test banning `DateTime.Now` outside `SystemClock`.
Use `DateTimeOffset` in the domain and `timestamptz` in Postgres; convert to the user's zone only in the UI.
Declare money as `decimal` with an explicit currency; add an architecture test banning `double` on money-named properties.
Add a `FakeClock` for tests so time-dependent logic is deterministic.

tasks.title: Human-readable number sequences
tasks.details: Generate MRN-1042, Study 001, RX-0114, RP-0114 and INV-0031 from a database sequence generator, never COUNT(*)+1, which races and duplicates under load.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent creation never produces duplicate business numbers
steps: Create a Postgres sequence per number type, e.g. `CREATE SEQUENCE patient.mrn_seq;`.
Add `INumberGenerator` in Application with `Task<string> NextAsync(string kind, CancellationToken)`.
Implement it in Infrastructure with `SELECT nextval('patient.mrn_seq')` and format as `MRN-{value:0000}`.
Repeat for study_number (`Study {n:000}`), prescription_number (`RX-{n:0000}`), report_number (`RP-{n:0000}`), bill_number (`INV-{n:0000}`).
NEVER use `COUNT(*) + 1` — two concurrent requests will produce the same number.
Keep the UNIQUE constraint on each column as the final backstop.
Test by generating 1000 numbers across parallel tasks and asserting no duplicates.

tasks.title: Choose data structures deliberately
tasks.details: Dictionary for in-loop lookups (never repeated FirstOrDefault, which is O(n^2)); HashSet for membership and permission set math; IReadOnlyList/IReadOnlyCollection on public APIs; records for DTOs and value objects; IAsyncEnumerable for streaming large instance lists; aggregates expose IReadOnlyCollection over a private List so invariants hold.
acceptanceCriteria: Collection types on public APIs are read-only and lookups are O(1)
steps: Audit existing loops for repeated `FirstOrDefault` inside a `foreach` — replace with a `ToDictionary` lookup built once.
Use `HashSet<string>` for permission checks and any 'have I seen this' test.
Change public API return types from `List<T>` to `IReadOnlyList<T>` / `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`.
Convert DTOs and value objects to `record` for structural equality and immutability.
Expose aggregate child collections as `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` over a private `List<T>` so callers cannot bypass invariants.
Use `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` when streaming large DICOM instance lists instead of materialising them.
Add these as review checklist items in `docs/code-review.md`.

sections.name: Local Infrastructure (Docker Compose / .NET Aspire)
sections.goal: One-command local environment: PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, and Seq running and reachable, with an optional .NET Aspire AppHost for orchestration.

tasks.title: Author docker-compose.yml for infrastructure
tasks.details: Create deploy/local/docker-compose.yml with services: postgres:17, redis:7, rabbitmq:3-management, datalust/seq. Add named volumes and a shared network.
acceptanceCriteria: `docker compose config` validates the file
steps: Create `docker-compose.yml` at the repo root.
Add a `postgres:16` service: env `POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/DB`, port `5432:5432`, named volume `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
Add `redis:7-alpine` on `6379:6379` — this backs the study lock and the SignalR backplane.
Add `rabbitmq:3-management` on `5672:5672` and `15672:15672` for the management UI.
Add a log/telemetry sink such as `datalust/seq` on `5341`/`8081`.
Add `azurite` for local blob storage of DICOM files.
Give every service a `healthcheck` block so dependents can wait for readiness.
Define a shared network `mediview-net` and attach all services.
Never hardcode production credentials; keep local values in `.env` and reference with `${VAR}`.

tasks.title: Bring up the local stack
tasks.details: Run `docker compose -f deploy/local/docker-compose.yml up -d`. Confirm containers healthy with `docker compose ps` and `docker compose logs -f`.
acceptanceCriteria: All four containers report healthy/running
steps: Run `docker compose up -d`.
Check status with `docker compose ps` — every container should read healthy, not just running.
Tail logs for failures: `docker compose logs -f postgres redis rabbitmq`.
If a port is already taken, change the HOST side of the mapping only (e.g. `5433:5432`).
Confirm volumes persist: `docker compose down`, then `up -d`, and verify data survived.
Document the commands in `README.md`.

tasks.title: Verify individual services via CLI
tasks.details: Fallback single commands: `docker run -d --name mv-postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=Pass@word1 -p 5432:5432 postgres:17`; `docker run -d --name mv-redis -p 6379:6379 redis:7`; `docker run -d --name mv-rabbitmq -p 5672:5672 -p 15672:15672 rabbitmq:3-management`; `docker run -d --name mv-seq -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -p 5341:80 datalust/seq`.
acceptanceCriteria: Each service reachable on its mapped port
steps: Postgres: `docker compose exec postgres psql -U mediview -d mediview -c "\l"`.
Redis: `docker compose exec redis redis-cli ping` should return `PONG`.
RabbitMQ: open http://localhost:15672 and log in with the compose credentials.
Seq: open http://localhost:8081 and confirm the ingestion endpoint responds.
Azurite: confirm the blob endpoint at http://localhost:10000 is reachable.
Write the results into `docs/local-setup.md` as a troubleshooting table.

tasks.title: Wire secrets with user-secrets and .env
tasks.details: Use `dotnet user-secrets` per service for connection strings/keys locally; provide a committed .env.example (no real secrets).
acceptanceCriteria: No secrets in source; .env.example documents required keys
steps: In each Api project run `dotnet user-secrets init`.
Add the connection string: `dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Default" "Host=localhost;Database=mediview;Username=mediview;Password=..."`.
Add the JWT signing key the same way — never in `appsettings.json`.
Create `.env.example` listing every variable name with placeholder values, and commit THAT.
Add the real `.env` to `.gitignore`.
Confirm `appsettings.json` contains no secret by grepping for `Password` and `Key`.
Document in README that production reads the same keys from Key Vault, so no code changes between environments.

tasks.title: Create optional .NET Aspire AppHost
tasks.details: Add an Aspire AppHost project to orchestrate services + containers with the dashboard; keep compose as the container-only fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: `dotnet run` on AppHost starts services with Aspire dashboard
steps: Create the AppHost: `dotnet new aspire-apphost -n MediView.AppHost -o src/AppHost`.
In `Program.cs`, declare resources: `builder.AddPostgres("postgres")`, `AddRedis("redis")`, `AddRabbitMQ("rabbit")`.
Add each service with `builder.AddProject<Projects.MediView_Patient_Api>("patient")`.
Wire dependencies with `.WithReference(postgres)` so connection strings inject automatically.
Run `dotnet run --project src/AppHost` and open the Aspire dashboard.
Keep docker-compose as the CI/deployment path — Aspire is a developer convenience, not a replacement.

tasks.title: Add local admin UIs (optional)
tasks.details: Optionally add pgAdmin and RedisInsight containers; document RabbitMQ management UI at http://localhost:15672 and Seq at http://localhost:5341.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin UIs reachable and documented in docs/local.md
steps: Add pgAdmin or Adminer to compose on port `8080` for browsing Postgres.
Add RedisInsight (or use `redis-cli`) to inspect lock keys while testing concurrency.
Confirm the RabbitMQ management UI shows exchanges and queues once MassTransit connects.
Put these under a compose `profiles: [tools]` block so `docker compose up` stays lean by default.
Start them on demand: `docker compose --profile tools up -d`.

tasks.title: Create the initial EF Core migration per service
tasks.details: For each service, write the IEntityTypeConfiguration classes for its schema and run `dotnet ef migrations add Init` then `dotnet ef database update`, so the generated DDL matches the reviewed baseline (schemas, CHECK constraints, unique join keys, FK indexes). Seed identity.roles, identity.permissions and the Admin account.
acceptanceCriteria: Every service creates its own schema from migrations and the seeded Admin can sign in
steps: Pick a service (start with Auth) and open its Infrastructure project.
Write the `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` classes for its aggregates first — migrations should never be generated from a half-modelled context.
Generate the migration: `dotnet ef migrations add Init -p src/Services/Auth/MediView.Auth.Infrastructure -s src/Services/Auth/MediView.Auth.Api`.
OPEN the generated migration file and read it — confirm the schema, CHECK constraints, unique indexes and FK indexes match the DBML.
Apply it: `dotnet ef database update -p ... -s ...`.
Verify in psql: `\dn` lists the schema and `\dt auth.*` lists the tables.
Repeat for every service, each writing into its OWN schema.
Add the seed for roles, permissions and the Admin account as an idempotent seeder that runs on startup in Development.
Commit migrations — they are source code, not build output.

tasks.title: One-command local environment
tasks.details: docker compose up must bring up postgres, redis, rabbitmq, the log/telemetry sink, the gateway, every service and the Blazor app, seeded and working end to end. Optionally add .NET Aspire for service discovery and the dashboard (it complements compose, it does not replace it in CI).
acceptanceCriteria: A fresh clone reaches a working system with a single command
steps: Extend `docker-compose.yml` with the application services: gateway, each Api, and the Blazor web app.
Use `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` so apps wait for Postgres and RabbitMQ.
Set `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development` and point connection strings at the compose service NAMES (`Host=postgres`), not localhost.
Run migrations automatically on startup in Development only, guarded by an environment check.
Seed demo data: one admin, two doctors with working hours, two patients with wallet balance, a sample DICOM study.
Test the real bar: `git clone`, `docker compose up`, open the browser, log in, and complete one booking.
Write the exact steps in `README.md` under 'Run locally'.
Fix anything that required a manual step — the goal is one command.

sections.name: Auth Microservice
sections.goal: A standalone Auth service issuing JWT access + refresh tokens over ASP.NET Core Identity, publishing UserRegistered, and exposing a shared token-validation config.

tasks.title: Scaffold Auth service in Clean Architecture
tasks.details: Create Auth.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects wired with BuildingBlocks. `dotnet new webapi` for Api (minimal APIs or controllers).
acceptanceCriteria: Auth service builds and runs with a health endpoint
steps: Generate the service from the template: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Auth -o src/Services/Auth`.
Confirm the four projects exist and reference inward only.
In Domain, create the `Users/` folder with `User.cs` as an AggregateRoot.
Give User: Id, Username, Email, PasswordHash, IsActive, FailedLoginCount, LockedUntil, and audit fields.
Add `IUserRepository.cs` in the same `Users/` folder.
In Application, create `Users/Commands/` and `Users/Queries/` folders.
In Api, add `Endpoints/AuthEndpoints.cs` with a `MapAuthEndpoints(this IEndpointRouteBuilder)` extension.
Build and add all four projects to the solution.

tasks.title: Add ASP.NET Core Identity + EF Core (Npgsql)
tasks.details: Configure Identity user/store on PostgreSQL via Npgsql. Add DbContext, run `dotnet ef migrations add InitAuth` and `dotnet ef database update`. Maps to auth.users (username/email unique, password_hash, is_active NOT NULL DEFAULT true, timestamptz audit columns).
acceptanceCriteria: Users table created in Postgres via EF migration
steps: Add packages to Infrastructure: `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore` and `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL`.
Create `AuthDbContext : IdentityDbContext<ApplicationUser, ApplicationRole, Guid>`.
In `OnModelCreating`, call `base.OnModelCreating(builder)` FIRST, then `builder.HasDefaultSchema("auth")`.
Rename the Identity tables to snake_case (`users`, `roles`, `user_claims`) so they match the rest of the schema.
Configure password rules in `AddIdentity`: minimum length 8, digit and uppercase required.
Enable lockout options: 5 failed attempts, 15-minute lockout.
Register with `AddDbContext<AuthDbContext>(o => o.UseNpgsql(cs, npg => npg.EnableRetryOnFailure()).UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention())`.
Generate and apply the migration, then confirm the `auth` schema exists in psql.

tasks.title: Issue JWT access + rotating refresh tokens
tasks.details: Issue short-lived JWT access tokens (~15 min) signed with a key from configuration / Key Vault. Use HS256 for a single issuer or RS256 (asymmetric) so any service or the gateway validates with the public key. Embed claims: sub (userId), email, role, permission claims, jti, iss, aud, exp. Issue long-lived refresh tokens stored hashed in the DB, single-use and rotated on each refresh, with server-side revocation. This internal JWT issuance is the DEFAULT auth provider (flag = internal); an external identity provider can be swapped in later behind the same flag.
acceptanceCriteria: Login returns a signed JWT carrying role/permission claims plus a rotating, revocable refresh token
Refresh tokens persist in auth.refresh_tokens hashed, single-use, with revoked_at/replaced_by_id
steps: Add `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt` to Infrastructure.
Create `JwtOptions` (Issuer, Audience, SigningKey, AccessTokenMinutes, RefreshTokenDays) and bind it from configuration with `ValidateOnStart()`.
Create `ITokenService` in Application with `GenerateAccessToken(user, roles, permissions)` and `GenerateRefreshToken()`.
Implement access tokens as JWTs with claims: `sub` (userId), `email`, `role`, one `permission` claim per permission, plus `jti`, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`.
Set the access token lifetime to about 15 minutes — short, because it cannot be revoked.
Use RS256: generate an RSA key pair, keep the private key in user-secrets/Key Vault and expose the public key so every service validates without sharing a secret.
Generate refresh tokens as 32+ bytes from `RandomNumberGenerator`, base64-encoded.
Store ONLY the SHA-256 hash in `auth.refresh_tokens` with `expires_at`; never store the raw token.
On refresh: look up by hash, reject if revoked/expired, issue a new pair, set `revoked_at` and `replaced_by_id` on the old one (single-use rotation).
Detect reuse: if a token that is already revoked is presented, revoke the WHOLE chain for that user — it means the token was stolen.

tasks.title: Register (Patient self-service) / Login / Refresh / Logout
tasks.details: Self-registration through Register creates a PATIENT account only. Login / Refresh / Logout work for every role. Admin and Doctor accounts are never self-registered (see the seeding and doctor-onboarding tasks).
acceptanceCriteria: End-to-end register->login->refresh->logout works
steps: Create `RegisterCommand(username, email, password, fullname)` and its handler.
In the handler, hard-code the role assignment to `Patient` — the endpoint must not accept a role from the request body.
Hash the password with the Identity password hasher; never write your own.
Create `LoginCommand` returning access + refresh tokens; on success reset `FailedLoginCount` and set `LastLoginAt`.
Return an identical generic error for 'unknown user' and 'wrong password' so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.
Create `RefreshTokenCommand` performing the rotation from the previous task.
Create `LogoutCommand` that revokes the presented refresh token (the access token simply expires).
Map the endpoints in `AuthEndpoints.cs`: `POST /auth/register`, `/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`.
Add validators for each command (email format, password policy).
Test the full cycle with curl or the .http file: register -> login -> call a protected endpoint -> refresh -> logout.

tasks.title: Publish UserRegistered integration event
tasks.details: On successful registration, publish UserRegistered via the message bus (see S16 bus setup) using the Outbox pattern.
acceptanceCriteria: UserRegistered observed on the broker after registration
steps: Reference `MediView.Contracts` from Auth.Infrastructure and Auth.Api.
Add MassTransit with the RabbitMQ transport in `AddInfrastructure`.
Enable the EF outbox: `o.AddEntityFrameworkOutbox<AuthDbContext>(c => c.UsePostgres())`.
In the Register handler, call `IPublishEndpoint.Publish(new UserRegistered(user.Id, user.Email, clock.UtcNow))` BEFORE `SaveChangesAsync`, so the message row commits in the same transaction.
Confirm in psql that the outbox table holds the message after the commit.
In the Patient service, add a `UserRegisteredConsumer` that creates the Patient profile and its MRN.
Make the consumer idempotent: if a patient already exists for that user id, return without error.
Test end to end: register a user, then confirm a row appears in `patient.patients`.
Kill the Patient service, register a user, restart it, and confirm the message is still delivered.

tasks.title: Ship a shared JWT validation extension
tasks.details: Provide an AddJwtAuth() extension configuring JwtBearer for every service and the gateway: ValidateIssuer, ValidateAudience, ValidateLifetime, ValidateIssuerSigningKey, a small ClockSkew, and (for RS256) the signing key / JWKS endpoint. Endpoints then use [Authorize] plus the permission policies from the Role service.
acceptanceCriteria: Any service validates Auth-issued JWTs through the shared extension
steps: In BuildingBlocks.Infrastructure add `AuthenticationExtensions.cs`.
Write `public static IServiceCollection AddJwtAuth(this IServiceCollection s, IConfiguration cfg)`.
Inside, call `AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme).AddJwtBearer(...)`.
Set `TokenValidationParameters`: ValidateIssuer, ValidateAudience, ValidateLifetime, ValidateIssuerSigningKey all true, and `ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)` (the 5-minute default is too loose).
Load the RSA public key for signature validation.
Add the `OnMessageReceived` event to read the token from the `access_token` query string when the path starts with `/hubs` — SignalR WebSockets cannot send an Authorization header.
Add `OnAuthenticationFailed` to log the reason at Warning (without the token itself).
Call `services.AddJwtAuth(Configuration)` from every Api project and the gateway.
Verify a token issued by Auth is accepted by the Patient service without any shared secret.

tasks.title: Seed Admin in the database; restrict self-registration
tasks.details: Seed the Admin account(s) directly in the database - admins are never self-registered. Enforce that the public Register endpoint can only create Patient accounts; Doctor and Admin roles are provisioned by an admin (see doctor onboarding).
acceptanceCriteria: Register only yields Patient accounts; an Admin exists from seed data
steps: Create `AuthDbSeeder` in Infrastructure with an idempotent `SeedAsync()`.
Seed the three roles (Admin, Doctor, Patient) using `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` semantics — check before insert.
Seed the permission list, marking `study.diagnose` as non-grantable to Admin.
Create the Admin user with a password read from configuration (never a literal in code) and assign the Admin role.
Run the seeder at startup in Development; in production run it as an explicit one-off command.
Add a guard in the Register handler: reject any request whose body attempts to set a role.
Add an integration test asserting `POST /auth/register` can never produce a Doctor or Admin account.
Verify the seeded Admin can log in and that no second Admin appears after restarting twice.

tasks.title: Account lockout and login telemetry
tasks.details: Track failed_login_count, locked_until and last_login_at on auth.users; lock the account temporarily after repeated failures and log attempts (without credentials).
acceptanceCriteria: Repeated bad passwords lock the account and the lock expires automatically
steps: On a failed login, increment `FailedLoginCount` and save.
When the count reaches 5, set `LockedUntil = clock.UtcNow.AddMinutes(15)`.
In the Login handler, check `LockedUntil` FIRST and return the generic failure without checking the password.
On a successful login, reset `FailedLoginCount` to 0, clear `LockedUntil`, and set `LastLoginAt`.
Log every attempt with the username and IP but NEVER the password or token.
Add rate limiting on `/auth/login` with ASP.NET's `AddRateLimiter` as a second layer of defence.
Test: 5 bad passwords lock the account; the 6th attempt with the CORRECT password still fails; after 15 minutes it succeeds.

sections.name: Role & Permission Microservice
sections.goal: Central role/permission management with policy-based authorization, default seeded roles (Patient, Doctor, Admin), and permission claims flowing into JWTs.

tasks.title: Scaffold Role service (Clean Architecture)
tasks.details: Create Role.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects and DbContext on Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Role service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Identity` to create the four projects -o src/Services/Identity` to create the four projects` (the template from S01-T09).
Create Domain folders: Roles/, Permissions/, Doctors/, Admins/.
Create `IdentityDbContext` with HasDefaultSchema("identity").
Add the project references and build.

tasks.title: Model roles, permissions, and assignments
tasks.details: Domain: Role, Permission, RolePermission, UserRole. Add EF config + `dotnet ef migrations add InitRole`. Maps to identity.roles, identity.permissions, identity.role_permissions and identity.user_roles (UNIQUE(user_id, role_id); user_id is a cross-service reference to auth.users, so no FK).
acceptanceCriteria: Role/permission schema migrated to Postgres
steps: Create Role, Permission, RolePermission, UserRole entities in Domain.
Add Admin and Doctor entities (Doctor holds license_number, department, specialty, is_verified, verified_by, verified_at).
Add DoctorCredential with kind, title, issuer, issued_at, document_url.
Write configurations: unique (role_id, permission_id), unique (user_id, role_id), unique license_number.
Make user_id a plain Guid with an `// xref: auth.users.id` comment - NO foreign key.
Add the `is_grantable` flag to Permission.
Create and apply the migration; verify constraints in psql.

tasks.title: Implement permission-based authorization
tasks.details: Add a custom IAuthorizationPolicyProvider + permission requirement/handler so `[HasPermission("studies.read")]` works across services.
acceptanceCriteria: Endpoints enforce fine-grained permissions
steps: Create `PermissionRequirement : IAuthorizationRequirement` holding a permission code.
Create `PermissionAuthorizationHandler : AuthorizationHandler<PermissionRequirement>` reading permission claims from the ClaimsPrincipal.
Create `PermissionPolicyProvider : IAuthorizationPolicyProvider` that builds a policy on demand from the policy name.
Register all three in DI via an `AddPermissionPolicies()` extension in BuildingBlocks.
Now `RequireAuthorization("study.diagnose")` works without pre-registering every policy.
Test with a token that lacks the permission and confirm 403.

tasks.title: Feed permissions into JWT claims
tasks.details: Coordinate with Auth so effective permissions are embedded as claims at token issuance (or resolved via a claims transformation).
acceptanceCriteria: JWT carries permission claims used by policies
steps: In the Auth token service, call Identity (gRPC or a direct query) to fetch the user's permission codes at login.
Add each as a claim: `new Claim("permission", code)`.
Keep the token small - if the list grows past ~30, switch to a roles claim plus a cached server-side lookup.
Cache the role->permissions map in Redis with a short TTL and invalidate on change.
Decode a token at jwt.io and confirm the permission claims are present.

tasks.title: Seed default roles and permissions
tasks.details: Seed Patient, Doctor, Admin with baseline permissions on startup (idempotent seeder).
acceptanceCriteria: Fresh DB contains the three default roles
steps: Write the seeder for the three roles: Admin, Doctor, Patient.
Seed the permission list: study.read, study.diagnose, study.status.change, study.status.override, image.import, doctor.onboard, bill.pay, audit.read, flags.manage.
Mark study.diagnose and study.status.override as is_grantable = false (server-enforced).
Grant Patient: study.read (own), bill.pay.
Grant Doctor: study.read, study.diagnose, study.status.change.
Grant Admin: everything EXCEPT study.diagnose.
Run the seeder and verify the matrix with a SQL query.

tasks.title: Admin endpoints for role management
tasks.details: CRUD for roles/permissions and assign/unassign to users, guarded by admin permission.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can manage roles via API with authorization
steps: Create endpoints: GET /roles, GET /permissions, POST /users/{id}/roles, DELETE /users/{id}/roles/{roleId}.
Protect them all with RequireAuthorization("roles.manage").
In the assign handler, reject any attempt to grant a permission where is_grantable = false.
Reject granting the Doctor role from this endpoint - it only comes from the onboarding flow.
Return the full matrix shape the admin UI needs (permission x role grid).
Write the audit entry for every grant/revoke.

tasks.title: Admin-only doctor onboarding with credential verification
tasks.details: An admin creates each doctor account and attaches proof of experience - certificates, awards, qualifications. The Doctor role is granted only after those credentials are attached/verified; doctors cannot self-register. Store the credential metadata and attachments on the doctor profile. Maps to identity.doctors (license_number varchar UNIQUE, is_verified/verified_by/verified_at) plus identity.doctor_credentials rows of kind certificate/award/degree/license with issuer, issued_at and document_url.
acceptanceCriteria: A doctor account can only be created by an admin and requires attached credentials
A doctor cannot be marked verified without a verifying admin and at least one credential row
steps: Create `CreateDoctorCommand` (user details + license, department, specialty).
In the handler, create the auth user via gRPC/event, create the Doctor row with is_verified = false.
Create `AddDoctorCredentialCommand` accepting an uploaded file; store the file in blob and save the URL.
Create `VerifyDoctorCommand`: require at least one credential row, set is_verified, verified_by, verified_at.
Only when verification succeeds, grant the Doctor role via the user_roles table.
Add a guard: a Doctor with is_verified = false cannot be assigned studies or appear in booking.
Test: create -> attempt to book (fails) -> attach credential -> verify -> now bookable.

tasks.title: Admin break-glass override (full permission, audited)
tasks.details: Admin holds full permission over every resource but uses it only as break-glass - for example correcting a patient's data or diagnosis when the assigned doctor is unavailable. Admin does NOT replace the doctor in the normal flow. Every admin override is written to the audit log with actor, reason, and before/after values. Overrides are written to audit.audit_log with actor, role, action, entity, reason, and before_data/after_data jsonb.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can override any patient/study data and every override is audited
steps: Define the override endpoints (e.g. PATCH /admin/studies/{id}/status) behind RequireAuthorization("study.status.override").
Make `reason` a REQUIRED field on the request and validate it is non-empty.
Before mutating, capture the current state as JSON (before_data).
After mutating, capture after_data and write one audit.audit_log row with actor, role, action, entity, reason, both snapshots, IP and correlation id.
Return 400 if reason is missing - the audit trail is not optional.
Verify by overriding a status and reading the audit row back.

tasks.title: Permission-based authorization policies
tasks.details: Authorize on permissions, not roles: RequireAuthorization("study.diagnose"). Roles map to permission sets; endpoints check permissions. Mark server-enforced permissions is_grantable = false so the admin matrix greys them out.
acceptanceCriteria: Endpoints declare permission policies and non-grantable permissions cannot be assigned
steps: Go through every endpoint and replace `[Authorize(Roles="Doctor")]` with `.RequireAuthorization("<permission>")`.
Build a table in docs mapping endpoint -> required permission.
Add the is_grantable flag to the API response so the admin matrix can grey those cells.
Add a fallback policy requiring an authenticated user so nothing is accidentally public.
Explicitly mark public endpoints with `.AllowAnonymous()` (login, register, health).
Test each role against each endpoint and record the result.

tasks.title: Admin must not hold study.diagnose
tasks.details: Seed the permission matrix so Admin holds every permission EXCEPT study.diagnose. Break-glass changes a study's status; it never makes an admin the author of a report. Enforce server-side, independent of the roles screen.
acceptanceCriteria: An admin calling the diagnose endpoint is refused even with break-glass enabled
steps: Open the seeder and confirm Admin is granted every permission EXCEPT study.diagnose.
Add a server-side guard in the diagnose handler: if the caller holds the Admin role, refuse regardless of claims.
Add the same check to report create/update/finalize - authorship must be a verified doctor.
Write the rationale as a comment: break-glass changes status, never authorship of a report.
Test with an admin token: opening the viewport read-only is fine, finalizing a report returns 403.
Reflect it in the UI matrix as a greyed, non-grantable cell.

sections.name: Patient & Studies Microservice
sections.goal: Patient and Study aggregates persisted per EF Core conventions, with a Study status lifecycle (todo / in-progress / re-diagnosis / done) as the single source of truth for the whole diagnosis workflow.

tasks.title: Scaffold Patient/Studies service
tasks.details: Create Patients.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects on Postgres with BuildingBlocks wiring.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Patient -o src/Services/Patient` (the template from S01-T09).
Create Domain folders: Patients/, Studies/, Diseases/.
Create `PatientDbContext` with HasDefaultSchema("patient").
Add references and build.

tasks.title: Model Patient and Study aggregates
tasks.details: Study is an aggregate root with StudyStatus enum (Registered, InReview, Locked, Reported, Closed), AuditableEntity fields, and assigned-doctors collection. A Study also carries a Status that drives the whole workflow (see the Study status state machine). Maps to patient.patients and patient.studies. Study carries the DICOM identifiers study_instance_uid (unique) and accession_number, the modality, appointment_id (cross-service), and diagnosis_status.
acceptanceCriteria: Domain enforces status transitions via methods
steps: Create `Patient.cs` as an AggregateRoot with UserId (xref), Mrn, PatientAnonymousName, BloodType.

Create `Study.cs` as an AggregateRoot with PatientId, StudyNumber, StudyInstanceUid, AccessionNumber, Modality, BodyPart, Laterality, Priority, StudyDate, Status, AppointmentId (xref), ParentStudyId, ImagesImportedAt.
Give Study a private constructor and a static `Create(...)` factory that assigns the number and raises StudyCreated.
Expose collections as IReadOnlyCollection over private lists (History, Diseases).
Add `Mrn` as a value object with a format guard.
Keep all mutations behind methods - no public setters.

tasks.title: Persist Patients/Studies with EF Core (per conventions)
tasks.details: Configure the Patients DbContext on Npgsql following the shared EF Core conventions: an IEntityTypeConfiguration per aggregate, Study mapped with its owned value objects, an xmin concurrency token, and EnableRetryOnFailure. Add the migration with `dotnet ef migrations add InitPatients` and apply it with `dotnet ef database update`.
acceptanceCriteria: Patients + Studies tables created in Postgres
steps: Write `PatientConfiguration` and `StudyConfiguration` implementing IEntityTypeConfiguration.
Map tables to the patient schema; make study_instance_uid and study_number unique.
Store enums as strings with HasConversion<string>() and a max length.
Map Mrn with OwnsOne; add xmin concurrency via `Property(x => x.Version).IsRowVersion()`.
Add indexes on patient_id, diagnosis_status, parent_study_id.
Run `dotnet ef migrations add InitPatients` and review the SQL before applying.
Apply with `dotnet ef database update` and verify with `\d patient.studies`.

tasks.title: Assign multiple doctors to a Study
tasks.details: Command to add/remove doctor assignments to a Study (many doctors allowed) with permission checks. Maps to patient.doctor_studies with UNIQUE(doctor_id, study_id) and an is_primary flag; doctor_id is a cross-service reference.
acceptanceCriteria: A Study can list multiple assigned doctors
steps: Create `DoctorStudy` entity with DoctorId (xref), StudyId, IsPrimary, AssignedAt.
Configure a unique index on (doctor_id, study_id).
Add `Study.AssignDoctor(doctorId, isPrimary)` enforcing at most one primary.
Create AssignDoctorCommand + endpoint POST /studies/{id}/doctors.
Reject assignment to an unverified doctor (query the local doctor directory replica).
Test assigning two doctors and confirm only one is primary.

tasks.title: Query endpoints for Studies list
tasks.details: Paged/filterable Studies list and Study detail endpoints using the specification pattern and PagedResult<T>.
acceptanceCriteria: Studies list returns paged, filtered results
steps: Create `GetWorklistQuery` with filters: status[], doctorId, dateFrom/dateTo, page, size.
Implement the handler with Dapper for the joined read model (studies + patient MRN + lock owner).
Write the SQL with a LEFT JOIN on study_locks WHERE released_at IS NULL to get the current holder.
Order by priority DESC then study_date, and page with LIMIT/OFFSET.
Return PagedResult<WorklistItemDto> - never entities.
Add the endpoint GET /studies with RequireAuthorization("study.read").
Check the generated SQL runs in a single round trip (no N+1).

tasks.title: Implement audit history
tasks.details: Record who changed what/when for Studies (audit log table or EF Core temporal tables) to satisfy compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Study change produces an audit record
steps: Confirm AuditableEntity stamps CreatedAt/UpdatedAt in SaveChangesAsync.
Add CreatedBy/UpdatedBy populated from the current user via an ICurrentUser service.
For clinical entities, ensure nothing is hard-deleted - add an IsDeleted flag and a global query filter.
Verify the filter with a query that must not return soft-deleted rows.

tasks.title: Consume UserRegistered to create Patient profile
tasks.details: Subscribe to UserRegistered and create/link a Patient profile idempotently.
acceptanceCriteria: New user results in a Patient profile
steps: In the Patient service Infrastructure, add a MassTransit consumer `UserRegisteredConsumer`.
In Consume, check whether a Patient already exists for that UserId (idempotency).
If not, generate the MRN via INumberGenerator and create the Patient profile.
Also create the patient's wallet by publishing/handling accordingly (or let Billing consume the same event).
Register the consumer in AddMassTransit configuration.
Test: register a user in Auth and confirm a Patient row with an MRN appears.
Replay the same message and confirm no duplicate is created.

tasks.title: Study status state machine: todo -> in-progress -> re-diagnosis -> done
tasks.details: Model Study.Status with values todo, in_progress, re_diagnosis, done and enforce the allowed transitions: todo -> in_progress when a doctor starts the read; in_progress -> done when the doctor finalizes with no further read; in_progress -> re_diagnosis when the doctor requests another read; re_diagnosis -> in_progress when a read resumes. Doctor-driven transitions require viewport lock ownership; an admin may override them (audited). Patient and doctor views both read this single status. Persist as patient.studies.diagnosis_status with a CHECK constraint over ('todo','in_progress','re_diagnosis','done'), defaulting to 'todo'.
acceptanceCriteria: Only allowed Study status transitions are accepted, guarded by role and lock ownership
diagnosis_status is CHECK-constrained in the database, not free text
steps: Create `StudyStatus` enum: Todo, InProgress, ReDiagnosis, Done.
In Study, add `private static readonly Dictionary<StudyStatus, StudyStatus[]> Allowed` describing legal transitions.
Write `Study.ChangeStatus(StudyStatus to, Guid actorId, ActorRole role, string? reason)`.
Inside, validate the transition against the map and throw/return a domain error if illegal.
Add guards: Todo->InProgress requires ImagesImportedAt != null AND the actor holds the lock; Doctor transitions require lock ownership.
Allow an Admin to bypass the map only when role == Admin AND reason is non-empty.
Configure the column with a CHECK constraint in the migration.
Write tests for every legal transition and at least three illegal ones.

tasks.title: Record every status transition in study_status_history
tasks.details: Write one patient.study_status_history row per transition: from_status, to_status, changed_by, changed_by_role (doctor/admin/system) and reason - reason being mandatory for admin break-glass overrides. This answers who moved a Study to re-diagnosis and why.
acceptanceCriteria: Every status change produces a history row with actor, role, and reason
steps: Create `StudyStatusHistory` entity: StudyId, FromStatus, ToStatus, ChangedBy, ChangedByRole, Reason, ChangedAt.
Inside Study.ChangeStatus, append a history row to the private collection - never from outside the aggregate.
Configure cascade delete from Study and an index on (study_id, changed_at DESC).
Require Reason when ChangedByRole is Admin (validate in the aggregate).
Add GET /studies/{id}/history returning the timeline for the UI.
Verify a status change writes exactly one history row.

tasks.title: Disease catalog and study findings
tasks.details: Model patient.diseases (ICD-10 code unique, name, reference_image_url) and patient.study_diseases linking findings to a Study with UNIQUE(study_id, disease_id). Note that modality belongs on the Study, not on the disease catalog.
acceptanceCriteria: Findings attach to a Study without duplicates and resolve to catalog diseases
steps: Create `Disease` entity (Code unique, Name, ReferenceImageUrl, Description) and seed a small ICD-10 subset.
Create `StudyDisease` join entity with a unique index on (study_id, disease_id).
Add `Study.AddFinding(diseaseId, note)` rejecting duplicates.
Add endpoints: GET /diseases (search by code/name) and POST /studies/{id}/findings.
Confirm modality lives on Study, not on Disease.
Test adding the same disease twice returns a domain error, not a duplicate row.

tasks.title: MRN and patient allergies
tasks.details: Add a unique MRN (Medical Record Number, e.g. MRN-1042) to patient.patients - it is the identifier shown throughout the UI. Model patient.patient_allergies (substance, reaction, severity) so the prescription composer can warn before an allergen is prescribed.
acceptanceCriteria: Every patient has a unique MRN and allergies are recorded per patient
steps: Add `Mrn` to Patient with a unique index and generate it from the sequence in the factory.
Create `PatientAllergy` entity: Substance, Reaction, Severity (mild/moderate/severe), NotedAt.
Configure it as part of the Patient aggregate with cascade delete and an index on patient_id.
Add `Patient.AddAllergy(...)` and endpoints POST/GET /patients/{id}/allergies.
Expose a query `GetAllergiesByPatient` that the Prescription service can call over gRPC.
Backfill MRNs for any existing rows in the migration.
Verify MRNs are unique and formatted (MRN-0001).

tasks.title: Study clinical attributes and follow-up chain
tasks.details: Add study_number, body_part, laterality, priority (routine/urgent/stat), referring_doctor_id, images_imported_at, and parent_study_id so a follow-up study links to the study it follows and the doctor can view both series side by side.
acceptanceCriteria: A follow-up study resolves its parent and the worklist can sort by priority
steps: Add StudyNumber, BodyPart, Laterality, Priority, ReferringDoctorId, ImagesImportedAt, ParentStudyId to Study.
Configure ParentStudyId as a self-referencing FK with an index.
Add `Study.CreateFollowUp(parentStudy, ...)` copying patient, modality and body part from the parent.
Add a guard preventing a study from being its own parent, and cap chain depth if you want.
Add GET /studies/{id}/chain returning the parent and children for the side-by-side view.
Update the worklist query to sort by Priority DESC so urgent/stat float to the top.
Create the migration and verify with a two-study follow-up chain.

tasks.title: Persist the viewport lock and its release reason
tasks.details: Redis stays the authoritative lock, but mirror it in patient.study_locks (study_id unique, doctor_id, acquired_at, last_heartbeat, expires_at, released_at, released_by, release_reason: manual/logout/ttl_expired/admin_force). This is what the UI shows (owner, elapsed, auto-release) and the audit trail for a forced release.
acceptanceCriteria: Every lock acquisition and release is durably recorded with its reason
steps: Create `StudyLock` entity: StudyId (unique), DoctorId, AcquiredAt, LastHeartbeat, ExpiresAt, ReleasedAt, ReleasedBy, ReleaseReason.
Create the `LockReleaseReason` enum: Manual, Logout, TtlExpired, AdminForce.
Configure a unique index on study_id (only one active lock) and an index on doctor_id.
In the lock service, write the row when Redis grants the lock and update ReleasedAt/ReleaseReason when it is released.
Treat Redis as authoritative: if Redis and the table disagree, Redis wins and the table is corrected.
Expose GET /studies/{id}/lock returning owner, acquired_at and expires_at for the UI banner.
Test all four release reasons produce the right row.

tasks.title: "Notify me when free" lock watchers
tasks.details: Model patient.lock_watchers (study_id, doctor_id, notified_at, unique per pair). When a lock releases, notify every watcher over SignalR and mark notified_at.
acceptanceCriteria: A watching doctor is notified within seconds of the lock releasing
steps: Create `LockWatcher` entity: StudyId, DoctorId, NotifiedAt, with a unique index on (study_id, doctor_id).
Add POST /studies/{id}/watch and DELETE /studies/{id}/watch endpoints.
In the lock-release path, load every watcher with NotifiedAt = null for that study.
Push a SignalR message to each watcher's user group and create a notification row.
Set NotifiedAt so a watcher is notified once per lock cycle, then clear watchers.
Test with two doctors: B watches, A releases, B is notified within seconds.

sections.name: Appointment / Booking Microservice
sections.goal: Checkup booking with availability, plus follow-up appointment scheduling triggered after a report is finalized.

tasks.title: Scaffold Booking service
tasks.details: Create Booking.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects on Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Booking -o src/Services/Booking` (the template from S01-T09).
Create Domain folders: Appointments/, WorkingHours/.
Create `BookingDbContext` with HasDefaultSchema("booking").
Build to confirm the layering.

tasks.title: Model Appointment, Slot, and FollowUp
tasks.details: Domain for appointment lifecycle (Requested, Confirmed, Completed, Cancelled) + availability slots. Add EF migration. Maps to booking.appointments (scheduled_start/scheduled_end, status booked/cancelled/completed/no_show, is_follow_up, parent_appointment_id) with UNIQUE(doctor_id, scheduled_start) so a slot cannot be double-booked.
acceptanceCriteria: Appointment schema migrated; transitions enforced
steps: Create `Appointment` AggregateRoot: PatientId, DoctorId, StudyId, ScheduledStart, ScheduledEnd, Status, IsFollowUp, ParentAppointmentId, Reason.
Create the `AppointmentStatus` enum: Booked, Cancelled, Completed, NoShow.
Add a CHECK that ScheduledEnd > ScheduledStart, and a UNIQUE index on (doctor_id, scheduled_start) to stop double-booking.
Add `Appointment.Cancel()`, `Complete()`, `MarkNoShow()` guarding legal transitions.
Configure ParentAppointmentId as a self-reference for follow-ups.
Create and apply the migration.

tasks.title: Booking + availability endpoints
tasks.details: Allow a patient to view availability and book a checkup; prevent double-booking with concurrency checks.
acceptanceCriteria: Patient can book an available slot; conflicts rejected
steps: Create `GetAvailableSlotsQuery(doctorId, date)`.
In the handler, load the doctor's working_hours rows for that day_of_week where the date is inside effective_from/effective_to.
Generate candidate slots by stepping start_time to end_time in slot_minutes increments.
Subtract slots that already have a Booked appointment.
Return only future slots (compare against IClock.UtcNow).
Add endpoints GET /doctors/{id}/slots?date= and POST /appointments.
In the booking handler, re-validate the slot server-side - never trust the slot the client posts.
Catch the unique-index violation and return 409 when two patients race for the same slot.

tasks.title: Follow-up scheduling from report
tasks.details: Consume ReportFinalized to offer/schedule a follow-up appointment date and publish FollowUpScheduled.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalized report enables a follow-up booking
steps: Add a consumer for `ReportFinalized` that reads follow_up_weeks.
If it is set, create a suggestion record (or just surface it) rather than auto-booking.
Create `BookFollowUpCommand(parentStudyId, doctorId, slot)`.
In the handler, create the appointment with IsFollowUp = true and ParentAppointmentId set.
Publish an event so the Patient service creates the follow-up Study with ParentStudyId.
Test the chain: finalize with follow_up_weeks -> patient books -> new study links to the old one.

tasks.title: Emit AppointmentBooked event
tasks.details: Publish AppointmentBooked (Outbox) for notification.
acceptanceCriteria: AppointmentBooked observed on broker
steps: Add the `AppointmentBooked` record to MediView.Contracts if not present.
Raise a domain event in Appointment.Create.
Publish the integration event through the outbox on save.
Have the Patient service consume it and create the Study in Todo status.
Verify in RabbitMQ that the message is published once per booking.

tasks.title: Doctor working hours & availability
tasks.details: Model each doctor's working hours. Patients can only book slots inside a doctor's working hours, and the doctor's dashboard lists exactly the studies booked within those hours. Admin or the doctor maintains the schedule. Model booking.working_hours as day_of_week + start_time + end_time + slot_minutes (NOT a free-text time range, which cannot be queried) and link via booking.doctor_working_hours with effective_from/effective_to.
acceptanceCriteria: Bookings are constrained to a doctor's working hours and surface on that doctor's dashboard
Availability is computed in SQL from structured day/time columns
steps: Create `WorkingHours` entity: DayOfWeek (0-6), StartTime, EndTime, SlotMinutes, Description.
Create `DoctorWorkingHours`: DoctorId (xref), WorkingHoursId, EffectiveFrom, EffectiveTo, unique on (doctor_id, working_hours_id).
Add CHECK constraints: day_of_week between 0 and 6, end_time > start_time, slot_minutes > 0.
Create admin/doctor endpoints to manage the schedule.
Rewrite availability to query these structured columns in SQL - this is why the free-text time_range had to go.
Reject any booking outside the doctor's hours in the command handler.
Test a booking one minute after end_time is refused.

sections.name: DICOM Imaging Microservice
sections.goal: Ingest, store, and serve DICOM: pixel data in Azure Blob Storage, metadata in the DB, linked to Studies, with DICOMweb-style (STOW/WADO/QIDO) endpoints via fo-dicom.

tasks.title: Scaffold Imaging service + add fo-dicom
tasks.details: Create Imaging.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects; add the fo-dicom package for parsing/serialization. This own-code DICOM handling is the DEFAULT import provider (flag = internal); a real PACS/modality can be plugged in later behind the same flag.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs; fo-dicom parses a sample .dcm
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Imaging -o src/Services/Imaging` (the template from S01-T09).
Add the fo-dicom package to Infrastructure (`dotnet add package fo-dicom`).
Create Domain folders: Series/, Instances/, Imports/.
Create `ImagingDbContext` with HasDefaultSchema("imaging").
Build and confirm fo-dicom resolves.

tasks.title: Configure blob + metadata storage
tasks.details: Store pixel data in Azure Blob Storage (Azurite locally) and DICOM metadata in Postgres. Add EF migration for image/instance metadata. Metadata maps to imaging.series (series_instance_uid unique) and imaging.instances (sop_instance_uid unique, rows/columns, transfer_syntax_uid, storage_path pointing at the blob); study_id is a cross-service reference.
acceptanceCriteria: Uploaded DICOM stored in blob with metadata row
steps: Add Azure.Storage.Blobs (Azurite locally) to Infrastructure.
Create `IDicomBlobStore` in Application with Upload/Download/Delete taking a storage key.
Implement `BlobDicomStore` writing to a container named `dicom`.
Choose a deterministic key layout: `{studyUid}/{seriesUid}/{sopUid}.dcm`.
Create Series and Instance entities holding the metadata plus StoragePath.
Store pixel data in blob and ONLY metadata in Postgres - never the file bytes in the database.
Create and apply the migration.

tasks.title: Implement STOW (store) endpoint
tasks.details: Accept DICOM upload, validate, extract metadata, persist, and associate with a Study id.
acceptanceCriteria: Uploaded instance linked to its Study
steps: Create the endpoint POST /studies/{studyUid}/instances accepting multipart/related or a plain file upload.
Parse each file with `DicomFile.OpenAsync(stream)`.
Read the tags: StudyInstanceUID (0020,000D), SeriesInstanceUID (0020,000E), SOPInstanceUID (0008,0018), Modality, Rows, Columns, WindowCenter/Width.
De-identify: overwrite PatientName with the anonymous name and drop identifying tags before storing.
Upload to blob, then upsert Series and Instance rows in one transaction.
Reject duplicates by SOPInstanceUID (unique index) and return 409.
Test with a sample .dcm file.

tasks.title: Serve WADO-RS + QIDO-RS for the Cornerstone viewer
