tasks.details: Serve WADO-RS (retrieve instances/frames) and QIDO-RS (query studies/series/instances) so the Blazor Cornerstone.js viewer can pull DICOM frames directly. Return frames in a Cornerstone-compatible form (DICOM P10 or rendered frames) and enable CORS for the front-end origin.
acceptanceCriteria: WADO-RS frames load in a Cornerstone.js test page
steps: Create WADO-RS endpoints: GET /studies/{uid}, /studies/{uid}/series/{uid}, and /instances/{uid}/frames/{n}.
Return `multipart/related; type=application/dicom` (or `application/octet-stream` for a single frame).
Create QIDO-RS search endpoints: GET /studies?PatientID=..., /studies/{uid}/series, returning DICOM JSON.
Add a CORS policy allowing the Blazor origin with credentials, since Cornerstone fetches directly.
Set caching headers on immutable frame responses.
Test by pointing a Cornerstone sample page at the endpoint and confirming an image renders.

tasks.title: Generate thumbnails / frame rendering
tasks.details: Produce cached preview images/frames (fo-dicom rendering) for fast viewport loading.
acceptanceCriteria: Thumbnail retrievable for a stored instance
steps: Add a thumbnail endpoint GET /instances/{uid}/thumbnail?size=128.
Use fo-dicom's DicomImage to render the frame to a bitmap.
Apply the stored window center/width so the thumbnail is not black.
Encode as JPEG/PNG and cache the result in blob so it is rendered once.
Return a placeholder rather than a 500 when rendering fails.

tasks.title: Admin "Import from X-ray" simulation
tasks.details: There is no physical modality, so provide an Import action (admin-triggered) that ingests a DICOM file/dataset and attaches its instances to the target Study - simulating an x-ray machine pushing images. After import the Study has images and is ready for a doctor to diagnose. Runs through the internal DICOM-import provider. Track each import as an imaging.import_jobs row: source (admin_upload/modality/pacs), imported_by, status, instance_count and error_message.
acceptanceCriteria: An admin can import a DICOM set into a Study, standing in for the x-ray machine
Each admin import creates an import_jobs row that reaches completed or failed
steps: Create the admin endpoint POST /admin/studies/{id}/import accepting multiple .dcm files.
Create an `ImportJob` row with status Pending and source AdminUpload before processing.
Process files (reuse the STOW path), incrementing instance_count and total_bytes.
Set status Completed with completed_at, or Failed with error_message.
Publish `StudyImagesImported` so the Patient service sets ImagesImportedAt.
Write an audit entry with the acting admin, the study and the instance count.
Require the image.import permission on the endpoint.
Test with a folder of sample instances and confirm the job reaches Completed.

tasks.title: Persist Cornerstone measurements
tasks.details: Store viewport annotations in imaging.annotations (instance_id, study_id, doctor_id, tool_type, tool_state jsonb) so measurements survive a reload and a second doctor can see them read-only while another holds the lock. Capture default window_center/window_width per instance.
acceptanceCriteria: Measurements reload with the study and render read-only for non-owners
steps: Create the `Annotation` entity: InstanceId, StudyId (xref), DoctorId (xref), ToolType, ToolState (jsonb).
Map ToolState with `.HasColumnType("jsonb")`.
Add endpoints POST/PUT/DELETE /studies/{id}/annotations and GET to load them all.
On the client, serialise Cornerstone tool state and save on change (debounced).
Require lock ownership to write; allow anyone with study.read to read.
Add the index on (study_id, instance_id).
Test: measure, reload the page, and confirm the measurement returns.

tasks.title: Import must not change study status
tasks.details: Importing images sets images_imported_at and instance counts but leaves the status at To do. The study only moves to In progress when a doctor opens it under lock. Enforce this in the import handler.
acceptanceCriteria: A study with imported images remains To do until a doctor opens it
steps: Open the import handler and confirm it never calls ChangeStatus.
Have it set only ImagesImportedAt and the instance counts on the study.
Add an assertion/test: import into a Todo study leaves it Todo.
Confirm the Todo->InProgress guard requires ImagesImportedAt to be set.
Show this rule in the admin import UI ('To do -> To do').

sections.name: Viewport Concurrency & Single-Doctor Distributed Lock
sections.goal: Enforce that only one Doctor edits a Study's Viewport at a time using a Redis distributed lock with ownership, TTL/heartbeat, and safe release; expose lock status to the UI.

tasks.title: Add Redis connection + RedLock
tasks.details: Wire StackExchange.Redis and RedLock.net (or a Redlock implementation) into a shared LockService abstraction (ILockService).
acceptanceCriteria: LockService connects to Redis and acquires a test lock
steps: Add StackExchange.Redis and RedLock.net to the Patient (or a shared) Infrastructure project.
Register `IConnectionMultiplexer` as a SINGLETON built from the configured connection string.
Create the RedLockFactory as a singleton over that multiplexer.
Add a health check for Redis.
Verify connectivity at startup with a PING.

tasks.title: Acquire lock on Viewport open
tasks.details: When a Doctor opens a Study viewport, acquire a lock keyed by study id with the doctor id as owner and a short TTL. Opening a Study for diagnosis also moves its status todo -> in_progress (see the Study status state machine).
acceptanceCriteria: First doctor acquires; Study status set to Locked
steps: Create `IStudyLockService` in Application: TryAcquireAsync, RenewAsync, ReleaseAsync, GetAsync.
Implement `RedisStudyLockService` using the key `study-lock:{studyId}` with the doctorId as the value and a 15-minute TTL.
Acquire with `SET key value NX PX 900000` semantics (RedLock handles this).
On success, write the StudyLock row and call Study.ChangeStatus(InProgress).
On failure, return the current owner so the caller can render the banner.
Create the endpoint POST /studies/{id}/lock.
Test two concurrent acquire calls - exactly one wins.

tasks.title: Heartbeat / auto-renew while active
tasks.details: Renew the lock via heartbeat while the doctor is active so it does not expire mid-session; stop renewing on idle.
acceptanceCriteria: Lock stays held during active use, expires after inactivity
steps: Add the endpoint POST /studies/{id}/lock/heartbeat.
In the handler, verify the caller is the current owner, then extend the Redis TTL and update LastHeartbeat/ExpiresAt.
Refuse (409) if the caller is not the owner.
On the client, call it every 30 seconds while the viewport is open.
Stop heartbeating when the tab is hidden for a long period so abandoned tabs expire.

tasks.title: Reject non-owners from write access
tasks.details: Any write/report action requires being the current lock owner; others receive 409 Conflict with owner info.
acceptanceCriteria: Second doctor is denied viewport write with clear conflict
steps: Create `StudyLockedException` carrying the owner id, owner name and lock age.
Write a small helper `EnsureLockOwner(studyId, doctorId)` used by every write path.
Call it in: save draft report, finalize, add finding, add annotation, change status.
Make the read paths deliberately NOT call it, so read-only viewing works.
Test each write endpoint with a non-owner token and confirm it is refused.

tasks.title: Safe release on close/timeout
tasks.details: Release lock on explicit close, logout, or TTL expiry; ensure only the owner can release (fencing token).
acceptanceCriteria: Lock released only by owner; auto-released on timeout
steps: Add the endpoint DELETE /studies/{id}/lock for an explicit release.
Release Redis with a Lua compare-and-delete so you only delete a lock you still own.
Update the StudyLock row: ReleasedAt, ReleasedBy, ReleaseReason = Manual.
Hook logout and viewport dispose (Blazor IAsyncDisposable) to call release with reason Logout.
Add a background service scanning for expired locks to write ReleaseReason = TtlExpired.
Test that closing the tab releases within the TTL.

tasks.title: Lock status API + events
tasks.details: Expose GET lock-status for a Study and publish StudyLocked/StudyUnlocked events for UI/notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: UI can query who holds a Study and react to events
steps: Add GET /studies/{id}/lock returning owner id, owner display name, acquired_at, expires_at and seconds remaining.
Publish `StudyLocked` / `StudyLockReleased` integration events on each change.
Wire these to the SignalR hub so connected clients update live.
Include the lock owner in the worklist read model so the list shows it without N calls.

tasks.title: Lock heartbeat, idle TTL and auto-release
tasks.details: The viewport heartbeats every ~30s to extend the lock; after ~15 minutes idle the lock auto-releases, the status stays as it was, and watchers are notified. Releases also happen on close and on logout.
acceptanceCriteria: An abandoned viewport releases its lock automatically after the TTL
steps: Set the TTL constant (15 minutes) in typed options, not a magic number.
Confirm the heartbeat extends ExpiresAt on every call.
Write the background `LockReaperService` (BackgroundService) running every minute.
In it, find StudyLock rows where ExpiresAt < now and ReleasedAt is null; release them with TtlExpired.
Leave the study status unchanged on expiry - only the lock is released.
Notify watchers and push LockReleased over SignalR.
Push a LockExpiring warning ~2 minutes before expiry so the doctor can extend.
Test by acquiring a lock and letting it idle past the TTL.

tasks.title: Return 409 with owner information on write attempts
tasks.details: Every write to a locked study returns 409 Conflict with the current owner and lock age in the body, so the UI can render the read-only banner with the holder's name.
acceptanceCriteria: Writing to a study locked elsewhere returns 409 naming the owner
steps: In the exception middleware, map StudyLockedException to 409.
Build the ProblemDetails body with extensions: ownerId, ownerName, lockedAt, expiresAt.
Ensure every write endpoint on a study can produce this response.
On the client, catch 409 and render the read-only banner with the owner's name.
Write an integration test asserting the 409 body contains the owner.

tasks.title: Admin force-release as an audited break-glass action
tasks.details: An admin can force-release another doctor's lock. It requires a reason, writes audit.audit_log with before/after, records release_reason = admin_force, and pushes the release over SignalR.
acceptanceCriteria: Force-release is refused without a reason and always audited
steps: Create the endpoint POST /admin/studies/{id}/lock/force-release requiring study.status.override.
Make `reason` required; return 400 when it is missing or blank.
Force-delete the Redis key (no owner check) and set ReleaseReason = AdminForce, ReleasedBy = admin.
Write the audit row with before/after and the reason.
Push LockReleased over SignalR so the displaced doctor's screen goes read-only immediately.
Show the displaced doctor a clear message explaining an admin released the lock.
Test end to end with two sessions.

sections.name: Real-time Collaboration (SignalR)
sections.goal: Live lock state, status changes and notifications pushed to the browser over SignalR, scaled across instances with a Redis backplane - announcements only, never the source of truth.

tasks.title: Stand up SignalR hubs
tasks.details: Add StudyHub (lock and status events for a study), WorklistHub (new imports and assignments) and NotificationHub (bell/toast). Hubs are [Authorize]d; the JWT arrives via the access_token query string for WebSockets, wired through OnMessageReceived.
acceptanceCriteria: An authenticated client connects and receives a test event
steps: Add the SignalR package to the service (or host hubs in the Api projects that own the data).
Create `Hubs/StudyHub.cs` inheriting Hub, decorated with [Authorize].
Create WorklistHub and NotificationHub the same way.
Map them in Program.cs: `app.MapHub<StudyHub>("/hubs/study")`.
Confirm AddJwtAuth includes the OnMessageReceived handler reading `access_token` from the query string for /hubs paths.
Add CORS with `.AllowCredentials()` for the Blazor origin.
Connect from a test client and confirm authentication succeeds.

tasks.title: Group-based subscriptions
tasks.details: Subscribe by group - study:{studyId}, doctor:{doctorId}, user:{userId} - never by raw connection id, so reconnects and multiple tabs behave.
acceptanceCriteria: Events reach every tab of the intended audience and nobody else
steps: Add hub methods `JoinStudy(Guid studyId)` and `LeaveStudy(Guid studyId)`.
Inside JoinStudy, CHECK the caller may read that study before adding them to the group.
Use `Groups.AddToGroupAsync(Context.ConnectionId, $"study:{studyId}")`.
On connect, add the user to `user:{userId}` and doctors to `doctor:{doctorId}` automatically.
Never key messages by connection id - a user with two tabs must receive both.
Test with two tabs and confirm both receive the event.

tasks.title: Redis backplane for scale-out
tasks.details: Add the Redis backplane so events reach clients on every instance. Without it a doctor connected to instance B never sees a release that happened on instance A.
acceptanceCriteria: With two instances running, an event on one reaches clients on the other
steps: Add the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.StackExchangeRedis package.
Chain it in DI: `services.AddSignalR().AddStackExchangeRedis(redisConnectionString)`.
Give the backplane a distinct channel prefix so it never collides with lock keys.
Run two instances locally on different ports.
Connect a client to each, trigger an event on one, and confirm the other client receives it.
This test is the whole point - without the backplane it silently fails only in production.

tasks.title: Push lock lifecycle events
tasks.details: Broadcast LockAcquired, LockExpiring (warning before TTL) and LockReleased to the study group, and notify lock watchers on release.
acceptanceCriteria: A second doctor's screen updates within seconds of a release
steps: Define the client-facing contract: LockAcquired, LockExpiring, LockReleased with a small payload.
Inject IHubContext<StudyHub> into the lock service (or handle the integration events).
After a successful acquire, send LockAcquired to `study:{id}` with owner name and expiry.
After release, send LockReleased and then notify each lock watcher in their `user:{id}` group.
From the reaper, push LockExpiring ~2 minutes before expiry to the owner only.
Test the full cycle with two browser sessions.

tasks.title: Push status and worklist updates
tasks.details: Broadcast StudyStatusChanged and StudyImported so the worklist and the patient status page update without a refresh.
acceptanceCriteria: Status changes appear live on both the doctor and patient screens
steps: Send StudyStatusChanged to `study:{id}` and to the doctor and patient groups.
Send StudyImported to the doctor's worklist group when an import completes.
On the client, update the row in place - do not refetch the whole list.
Debounce UI updates so a burst of events does not thrash rendering.
Test that the patient status page updates without a refresh.

tasks.title: The hub never grants authority
tasks.details: Redis holds the authoritative lock; the hub only announces. A dropped or spoofed socket must never grant, extend, or release a lock, and every hub method re-checks permissions server-side.
acceptanceCriteria: Disconnecting or replaying hub messages cannot change lock ownership
steps: Review every hub method: none of them may acquire, extend, or release a lock.
Re-check permissions inside each hub method - a connected client can call anything.
Confirm the lock service is the only writer of Redis lock keys.
Add a test simulating a spoofed hub call and assert lock ownership is unchanged.
Write the rule as a comment at the top of StudyHub: this hub announces, it never authorises.

tasks.title: Reconnection and state resync
tasks.details: Automatic reconnect with backoff on the client; on reconnect, re-fetch study state so a missed event cannot leave a stale read-only banner.
acceptanceCriteria: A network blip leaves the viewport showing correct lock state
steps: Configure the client with `.WithAutomaticReconnect(new[]{0,2,10,30 seconds})`.
Handle Reconnected: rejoin every group and re-fetch the current study and lock state.
Handle Closed: show a clear 'reconnecting' indicator and disable write actions.
Treat server state as truth on reconnect so a missed event cannot leave a stale banner.
Test by stopping the server briefly and confirming the UI recovers correctly.

sections.name: Reporting / Diagnosis Microservice
sections.goal: Doctors write and finalize a diagnosis Report against a Study (only the lock owner may write); finalized reports notify the patient and unlock downstream flows.

tasks.title: Scaffold Reporting service
tasks.details: Create Reporting.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects on Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Reporting -o src/Services/Reporting` (the template from S01-T09).
Create Domain folder Reports/ and `ReportingDbContext` with HasDefaultSchema("reporting").
Confirm the four projects reference inward only: Api -> Infrastructure -> Application -> Domain.
Add `Report.cs` as an AggregateRoot with Status, Findings, Impression, Decision, FinalizedAt.
Add `IReportRepository.cs` beside it in the Reports/ folder.
Register the DbContext with Npgsql, EnableRetryOnFailure and snake_case naming.
Add the project to the solution and run `dotnet build`.

tasks.title: Model Report and Diagnosis
tasks.details: Report aggregate linked to Study with Draft/Finalized states and diagnosis fields. Add EF migration. Maps to reporting.reports: status draft/finalized, findings, conclusion, decision (done/re_diagnosis), pdf_url and finalized_at, with a CHECK that a finalized report always carries a decision and a finalized_at.
acceptanceCriteria: Report schema migrated; state machine enforced
steps: Create `Report` AggregateRoot: StudyId (xref), DoctorId (xref), ReportNumber, Status, Findings, Impression, Decision, IsCritical, CriticalAckAt, FollowUpWeeks, PdfUrl, FinalizedAt.
Create the ReportStatus (Draft, Finalized) and ReportDecision (Done, ReDiagnosis) enums.
Add a CHECK: status = 'draft' OR (decision IS NOT NULL AND finalized_at IS NOT NULL).
Add `Report.SaveDraft(...)` and `Report.Finalize(decision, clock)` with the guard that a finalized report cannot be re-finalized.
Index study_id; make report_number unique.
Create and apply the migration.

tasks.title: Enforce lock ownership on write
tasks.details: Save/update report only if the caller currently owns the Study lock (call ILockService/lock-status).
acceptanceCriteria: Non-owners cannot create or edit a report
steps: Inject a lock checker (gRPC call to the Patient service or a shared service).
Call EnsureLockOwner at the start of SaveDraft, Finalize, and addendum creation.
Return 409 with owner details when the caller is not the holder.
Allow GET of a draft report for read-only viewers.
Test writing as a non-owner is refused while reading succeeds.

tasks.title: Draft save, finalize, and set the diagnosis decision
tasks.details: Draft-save and finalize the report. Finalizing records the doctor's decision and sets the Study status accordingly: no further read -> done; another read needed -> re_diagnosis. The decision is what the patient ultimately sees.
acceptanceCriteria: Draft->Finalize flow updates Study status
steps: Create SaveDraftCommand and FinalizeReportCommand.
SaveDraft upserts findings/impression, keeping status Draft.
Finalize requires a decision, sets FinalizedAt and the report number, and marks the report immutable.
Map Decision -> study status: Done -> Done, ReDiagnosis -> ReDiagnosis.
Raise ReportFinalized carrying StudyId, DoctorId, Decision, FollowUpWeeks and IsCritical.
Add the endpoints PUT /reports/{id}/draft and POST /reports/{id}/finalize.
Test both decision paths and confirm the study status follows.

tasks.title: Publish ReportFinalized event
tasks.details: On finalize, publish ReportFinalized (Outbox) consumed by Booking, Prescription, and Notification.
acceptanceCriteria: ReportFinalized observed on broker
steps: Confirm the `ReportFinalized` record exists in MediView.Contracts.
Publish it through the transactional outbox in the same transaction as the report update.
Add consumers: Patient (status), Prescription (issue), Billing (diagnosis fee), Notification (email).
Make each consumer idempotent by checking whether its effect already happened.
Verify one finalize produces exactly one message and four effects.

tasks.title: Export the diagnosis result as PDF
tasks.details: Export the finalized diagnosis result as a PDF the patient receives.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalized report downloadable as PDF
steps: Add QuestPDF (or another server-side PDF library) to Infrastructure.
Create `IReportPdfGenerator` in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.
Compose the document: hospital header, patient MRN and anonymous name, study details, findings, impression, doctor name and licence, finalized timestamp.
Render to a byte array, upload to blob, and store the URL on the report.
Add GET /reports/{id}/pdf streaming the file with the correct content type.
Log the export to audit.access_log (action = export_pdf).
Generate one and open it to check layout.

tasks.title: Findings + impression, critical results, follow-up
tasks.details: Structure the report as findings then impression (radiology convention). Add is_critical with an acknowledgement timestamp for critical findings, and follow_up_weeks, which drives the patient's "book follow-up" prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: A critical report is flagged and tracked until acknowledged
steps: Split the text fields into Findings and Impression in the entity, API and UI.
Add IsCritical plus CriticalAckAt, and an endpoint POST /reports/{id}/acknowledge.
When IsCritical is set on finalize, publish a high-priority notification and keep it open until acknowledged.
Add FollowUpWeeks (nullable int) with a sensible range validator.
Surface unacknowledged critical results on the admin dashboard.
Test that a critical report stays flagged until acknowledged.

tasks.title: Addenda instead of editing a finalized report
tasks.details: A finalized report is never edited in place. Corrections are appended to reporting.report_addenda with their own author and timestamp - standard radiology practice and a defensible audit position.
acceptanceCriteria: Editing a finalized report is refused; an addendum is created instead
steps: Create the `ReportAddendum` entity: ReportId, DoctorId, Body, CreatedAt.
Configure cascade delete from Report and an index on report_id.
Add POST /reports/{id}/addenda requiring a verified doctor.
In SaveDraft, reject any edit when Status is Finalized, returning an error that points to the addendum endpoint.
Include addenda in the PDF, clearly separated and timestamped.
Test: finalize, attempt an edit (refused), add an addendum (succeeds).

tasks.title: Finalize as one orchestrated transaction
tasks.details: Finalizing must: set the decision, move the study status (done or re_diagnosis), export the result PDF, issue the attached prescription, raise the diagnosis-fee bill, release the lock, and notify the patient. The local changes commit in one transaction with an outbox event; the rest happens on ReportFinalized.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalize either completes fully or leaves no partial state
steps: List everything finalize must do: set decision, move status, export PDF, issue prescription, raise the bill, release the lock, notify.
Keep LOCAL work in one transaction: report update + outbox message.
Move remote effects to consumers of ReportFinalized - do not call other services synchronously here.
Release the lock after the local commit succeeds.
Make the whole path idempotent so a retry cannot double-issue a prescription or bill.
Test the failure case: kill the process right after commit and confirm the outbox relays on restart, leaving no partial state.

sections.name: Prescription Microservice
sections.goal: Create prescriptions from a finalized report, referencing a drug catalog, and publish PrescriptionIssued for the cart/billing flow.

tasks.title: Scaffold Prescription service
tasks.details: Create Prescription.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects on Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Prescription -o src/Services/Prescription` (the template from S01-T09).
Create Domain folders Drugs/ and Prescriptions/, and `PrescriptionDbContext` with schema "prescription".
Confirm references point inward only.
Add `Prescription.cs` (AggregateRoot) with its Items collection exposed as IReadOnlyCollection.
Add `Drug.cs` for the formulary and the matching repository interfaces.
Register the DbContext with Npgsql, retry and snake_case naming.
Add to the solution and run `dotnet build`.

tasks.title: Model Prescription + items + drug catalog
tasks.details: Prescription aggregate with PrescriptionItem lines referencing a Drug catalog. Add EF migration and seed a sample catalog. Maps to prescription.prescriptions and prescription.prescription_items, where each item references prescription.drugs and snapshots drug_name and unit_price at issue time (items with no drug reference cannot be billed).
acceptanceCriteria: Prescription schema migrated; catalog seeded
Every prescription item resolves to a catalog drug and carries a priced quantity
steps: Create `Drug` (Code unique, Name, Form, Strength, Unit, UnitPrice, IsActive).
Create `Prescription` AggregateRoot: StudyId, ReportId, PrescribedBy, PrescriptionNumber, Status, Description, PdfUrl, IssuedAt.
Create `PrescriptionItem` inside the aggregate: DrugId, DrugName snapshot, UnitPrice snapshot, Dosage, Frequency, Duration, Quantity.
Add `Prescription.AddItem(drug, dosage, frequency, duration, quantity)` copying name and price at that moment.
Add a CHECK that quantity > 0 and expose items as IReadOnlyCollection.
Create and apply the migration; seed a small formulary.

tasks.title: Create prescription from finalized report
tasks.details: Consume ReportFinalized (or a doctor action) to create a prescription tied to the report/patient.
acceptanceCriteria: Finalized report can yield a prescription
steps: Add a `ReportFinalized` consumer.
Find the draft prescription attached to that report; if none, do nothing.
Set Status = Issued, assign the prescription number and IssuedAt.
Guard idempotency: if already Issued, return without changes.
Publish `PrescriptionIssued` with the items and the total.
Test finalize -> prescription becomes Issued exactly once.

tasks.title: Publish PrescriptionIssued
tasks.details: Publish PrescriptionIssued (Outbox) so Cart can offer the drugs for purchase.
acceptanceCriteria: PrescriptionIssued observed on broker
steps: Confirm the `PrescriptionIssued` contract carries PrescriptionId, PatientId, StudyId, items and total.
Publish it through the outbox.
Have Billing consume it to make the cart available, and Notification consume it to alert the patient.
Verify the message shape in RabbitMQ.

tasks.title: Export prescription as PDF
tasks.details: Export the issued prescription as a PDF the patient receives alongside the diagnosis result.
acceptanceCriteria: A finalized prescription can be exported as a PDF for the patient
steps: Reuse the PDF generator abstraction from Reporting.
Compose the prescription layout: patient, doctor and licence, date, each drug with dose/frequency/duration/quantity.
Upload to blob and store the URL on the prescription.
Add GET /prescriptions/{id}/pdf and log the export to the access log.
Generate one and check it is legible and complete.

tasks.title: Formulary catalog with form and strength
tasks.details: Model prescription.drugs with code, name, form (tablet/capsule/syrup/injection), strength, unit and unit_price - the formulary shown in the composer. Items snapshot drug_name and unit_price at issue time so a later price change never rewrites history.
acceptanceCriteria: Issued prescription items keep the price they were issued at
steps: Add Form and Strength to Drug and expose a search endpoint GET /drugs?q= for the composer.
Index name for search; filter out IsActive = false.
Confirm items snapshot DrugName and UnitPrice at issue time so later price changes never rewrite history.
Write a test: issue a prescription, change the drug price, and assert the issued item price is unchanged.

tasks.title: Allergy warning in the prescription composer
tasks.details: Before a drug is added, check the patient's recorded allergies and warn the doctor. The warning is advisory, and overriding it is recorded on the prescription.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding a known allergen raises a warning the doctor must acknowledge
steps: Add a gRPC (or HTTP) client to fetch the patient's allergies from the Patient service.
In AddItem, compare the drug name and its ingredient/class against the allergy list.
Return a warning payload rather than blocking - the doctor decides.
If the doctor proceeds, record the acknowledgement (who, when, which allergen) on the prescription.
Show the warning prominently in the composer UI.
Test with a patient allergic to a seeded drug.

sections.name: Cart & Billing / Payment Microservice
sections.goal: Patients add prescribed drugs to a cart, check out to create a bill, complete payment (test gateway), and receive order history; publishes BillPaid.

tasks.title: Scaffold Cart/Billing service
tasks.details: Create Cart.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects on Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Billing -o src/Services/Billing` (the template from S01-T09).
Create Domain folders Carts/, Bills/, Wallets/ and `BillingDbContext` with schema "billing".
Confirm references point inward only.
Add `Cart.cs`, `Bill.cs` and `Wallet.cs` as separate aggregate roots (never one giant root).
Declare all money properties as `decimal`, never `double`.
Register the DbContext with Npgsql, retry and snake_case naming.
Add to the solution and run `dotnet build`.

tasks.title: Model Cart, Order, and Invoice
tasks.details: Cart with line items, Order, Invoice/Bill with totals and payment status. Add EF migration. Add a patient wallet / account balance funded per patient; paying a bill debits the wallet. Maps to billing.wallets (balance CHECK >= 0), billing.bills (status unpaid/paid/cancelled/refunded), billing.bill_items, billing.payments (provider internal_wallet/external_gateway) and billing.wallet_transactions (top_up/payment/refund with balance_after).
acceptanceCriteria: Cart/Order/Invoice schema migrated
steps: Create `Wallet` AggregateRoot: PatientId (unique xref), Balance, Currency, with a CHECK balance >= 0.
Create `WalletTransaction`: Type (TopUp/Payment/Refund), Amount, BalanceAfter, PaymentId, Description.
Create `Bill`: BillNumber, PatientId, StudyId, CartId, Kind, TotalAmount, Status, PaidAt.
Create `BillItem` and `Payment` (Provider, ExternalReference, IdempotencyKey, Amount, Status, PaidAt).
Use decimal(14,2) for money everywhere - never double.
Create and apply the migration.

tasks.title: Populate cart from prescription
tasks.details: Consume PrescriptionIssued so prescribed drugs can be added to the patient's cart.
acceptanceCriteria: Prescribed drugs appear as add-to-cart options
steps: Add a `PrescriptionIssued` consumer that creates a Cart in status Open for that patient and prescription.
Copy each prescription item into a CartItem with the snapshot price and the FIXED quantity.
Add a unique index on (cart_id, prescription_item_id).
Add GET /carts/current and DELETE /carts/{id}/items/{itemId} (removing a line is allowed).
Reject any request that changes a quantity.
Test that the cart matches the prescription exactly.

tasks.title: Checkout creates a bill
tasks.details: Checkout creates the bill from the prescription (plus any diagnosis fee). Paying becomes available once the doctor has finalized the diagnosis.
acceptanceCriteria: Checkout produces an invoice with correct totals
steps: Create CheckoutCommand for the cart.
In the handler, recompute every line total server-side from the stored snapshot prices - never trust client totals.
Create a Bill of kind PrescriptionOrder with a generated BillNumber, copy the lines into BillItems, and set the cart to Ordered.
Return the bill for payment.
Test that tampering with a posted total has no effect.

tasks.title: Pay the bill from the patient wallet (internal, pluggable)
tasks.details: Pay the bill by debiting the patient's wallet balance - the DEFAULT internal payment provider (flag = internal). A real external payment gateway can be plugged in later behind the same flag without changing callers.
acceptanceCriteria: A test payment marks the bill Paid
Paying debits the wallet atomically and writes a wallet_transactions row with balance_after
steps: Create `IPaymentProvider` in Application with PayAsync(bill, idempotencyKey).
Implement `WalletPaymentProvider`: load the wallet with a row lock, check the balance, debit, append the transaction, mark the bill Paid.
Do the debit, ledger row and bill update in ONE database transaction.
Return a domain error (not an exception) for insufficient funds.
Add a stub `ExternalGatewayPaymentProvider` that throws NotImplemented for now.
Select the implementation by the payment.provider.external feature flag, defaulting to internal.
Test paying with a balance that is too low leaves the balance untouched.

tasks.title: Publish BillPaid + order history
tasks.details: On payment, settle the visit. If the doctor set the Study to re_diagnosis, keep it open for another read instead of closing; a done Study with a paid bill completes the journey.
acceptanceCriteria: BillPaid emitted; history endpoint returns orders
steps: Publish `BillPaid` through the outbox after a successful payment.
Have Notification consume it to confirm to the patient.
If the bill is the diagnosis fee and the study is Done, the visit is complete; if the study is ReDiagnosis, keep it open.
Add GET /patients/{id}/bills and /patients/{id}/orders for history.
Verify both bill kinds appear separately in history.

tasks.title: Cart restricted to an issued prescription
tasks.details: Model billing.carts and billing.cart_items. Only medications from an ISSUED prescription may enter the cart and quantities are fixed by the prescription - the patient can remove a line but never change a dose or quantity.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding an arbitrary drug or editing a quantity is rejected
steps: In the cart creation path, assert the prescription Status is Issued - refuse Draft.
Reject adding any drug not present on that prescription.
Reject quantity edits at the API level, not just in the UI.
Return a clear error code the UI can display.
Write three tests: arbitrary drug refused, quantity edit refused, removal allowed.

tasks.title: Separate diagnosis-fee and prescription-order bills
tasks.details: Bills carry a kind (diagnosis_fee raised on finalize, prescription_order raised on checkout) and a human-readable bill_number such as INV-0031, so the patient sees them as distinct invoices.
acceptanceCriteria: The diagnosis fee and the medication order are separate, numbered bills
steps: Add the `BillKind` enum (DiagnosisFee, PrescriptionOrder) to the Bill entity.
Raise the DiagnosisFee bill from the ReportFinalized consumer, using a configured fee amount.
Raise the PrescriptionOrder bill at checkout.
Generate BillNumber from the sequence (INV-0001).
Ensure the patient's bill list shows them as two distinct invoices.
Test that finalizing creates exactly one diagnosis-fee bill.

tasks.title: Idempotent payment and an append-only wallet ledger
tasks.details: Require an Idempotency-Key on payment POSTs, stored unique on billing.payments, so a retry never double-charges. Every wallet movement appends a wallet_transactions row carrying balance_after; the debit and the ledger row commit in one transaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Replaying a payment request charges exactly once and the ledger reconstructs the balance
steps: Require the `Idempotency-Key` header on POST /bills/{id}/pay and reject the request when missing.
Store it in Payment.IdempotencyKey with a UNIQUE index.
In the handler, look the key up first: if a payment already exists, return that result instead of charging again.
Catch the unique-violation race and return the existing payment.
Confirm every wallet movement writes BalanceAfter so the ledger reconstructs the balance.
Test: send the same payment request twice and assert the balance drops once.

tasks.title: Wallet top-up
tasks.details: Let a patient add funds to the wallet (internal provider now), recorded as a top_up transaction.
acceptanceCriteria: A top-up raises the balance and appends a ledger row
steps: Add the endpoint POST /wallets/{id}/topup with an amount.
Validate the amount is positive and within a sane cap.
Credit the balance and append a TopUp transaction in one transaction.
Since the external gateway is stubbed, treat top-up as an internal simulated credit and say so in the UI.
Test that the balance and ledger agree after several top-ups.

sections.name: Notification Microservice
sections.goal: React to domain events (report ready, appointment booked, bill paid, follow-up scheduled) and notify patients via email/SMS with templated messages and a delivery log.

tasks.title: Scaffold Notification service
tasks.details: Create Notification.Domain/Application/Infrastructure/Api projects on Postgres.
acceptanceCriteria: Service runs with health endpoint
steps: Generate the service: `dotnet new mediview-service -n Notification -o src/Services/Notification` (the template from S01-T09).
Create `NotificationDbContext` with schema "notification".
Confirm references point inward only.
Add `Notification.cs` with Channel, Status, RelatedType/RelatedId and SentAt.
Register the DbContext with Npgsql, retry and snake_case naming.
Add to the solution and run `dotnet build`.

tasks.title: Subscribe to domain events
tasks.details: Consume ReportFinalized, AppointmentBooked, BillPaid, FollowUpScheduled from the bus.
acceptanceCriteria: Each event triggers a notification workflow
steps: Add MassTransit consumers for ReportFinalized, PrescriptionIssued, BillPaid, AppointmentBooked and StudyStatusChanged.
Map each event to a template with a subject and body.
Resolve the recipient's email/phone by calling Auth over gRPC, or from a local replica.
Make consumers idempotent - dedupe on the event id.
Test that finalizing a report queues exactly one patient notification.

tasks.title: Integrate email/SMS provider
tasks.details: Integrate Azure Communication Services or SendGrid for email (and optional SMS) with templated content.
acceptanceCriteria: A test event sends a templated email
steps: Create `IEmailSender` and `ISmsSender` in Application.
Implement a development sender that writes to the log or a local file - no real provider needed yet.
Add a real implementation behind configuration for later (SendGrid/ACS).
Wrap sends in a Polly retry with backoff.
Never put PHI in a subject line - reference the study number, not the diagnosis.

tasks.title: Persist a notification/delivery log
tasks.details: Record sent notifications, status, and retries for audit and troubleshooting. Maps to notification.notifications (channel email/sms/in_app, related_type/related_id, status pending/sent/failed, sent_at).
acceptanceCriteria: Notifications are logged with delivery status
steps: Create the `Notification` entity: UserId, Channel, Subject, Body, RelatedType, RelatedId, Status, ErrorMessage, ReadAt, SentAt.
Write a row BEFORE sending with status Pending.
Update to Sent with SentAt, or Failed with ErrorMessage.
Add GET /notifications for the in-app bell and POST /notifications/{id}/read.
Push new in-app notifications over the NotificationHub.
Index (user_id, created_at DESC) for the bell query.

sections.name: API Gateway (YARP)
sections.goal: A single ingress via YARP with per-service routing, JWT auth forwarding, rate limiting, CORS, and aggregated health.

tasks.title: Create YARP gateway project
tasks.details: `dotnet new web` gateway; add YARP reverse proxy package and base configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Gateway starts and proxies a sample route
steps: Run `dotnet new web -n MediView.Gateway -o src/Gateway/MediView.Gateway`.
Add the Yarp.ReverseProxy package.
In Program.cs add `builder.Services.AddReverseProxy().LoadFromConfig(builder.Configuration.GetSection("ReverseProxy"))`.
Add `app.MapReverseProxy()`.
Add it to the solution and build.

tasks.title: Configure routes and clusters per service
tasks.details: Map routes to Auth, Role, Patients, Booking, Imaging, Reporting, Prescription, Cart, Notification clusters.
acceptanceCriteria: Each service reachable behind the gateway path
steps: In appsettings.json create the ReverseProxy section with Routes and Clusters.
Add one route per service with a path prefix: /api/auth/{**catch-all} -> auth cluster.
Add clusters for auth, identity, patient, booking, imaging, reporting, prescription, billing, notification.
Use container names as destination addresses in Docker (http://auth-api:8080).
Add a transform stripping the /api/{service} prefix before forwarding.
Route SignalR hub paths with WebSocket support enabled.
Test each route returns the right service's health endpoint.

tasks.title: Enforce JWT auth at the edge
tasks.details: Validate tokens at the gateway (shared AddJwtAuth) and forward identity/claims downstream.
acceptanceCriteria: Protected routes require a valid token at the gateway
steps: Call AddJwtAuth in the gateway so tokens are validated once at the edge.
Add `app.UseAuthentication()` and `app.UseAuthorization()` before MapReverseProxy.
Set a default authorization policy on routes, with AllowAnonymous on /api/auth/login and register.
Forward the validated identity downstream via headers or by passing the original token.
Confirm services still validate the token themselves - defence in depth, never trust the edge alone.

tasks.title: Add rate limiting and CORS
tasks.details: Apply ASP.NET Core rate limiting policies and a CORS policy for the Blazor origin.
acceptanceCriteria: Excess requests are throttled; Blazor origin allowed
steps: Add rate limiting: `builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(...)` with a fixed or sliding window per user/IP.
Apply a stricter limit to /api/auth/login to slow credential stuffing.
Add a CORS policy naming the Blazor origin, with AllowCredentials for SignalR.
Return 429 with a Retry-After header.
Test by exceeding the limit with a loop.

tasks.title: Aggregate health and expose OpenAPI
tasks.details: Add health-check aggregation and (optionally) a unified OpenAPI/Swagger surface.
acceptanceCriteria: /health reflects downstream service health
steps: Add AddHealthChecks in the gateway with a check per downstream service.
Map /health/live and /health/ready.
Aggregate the OpenAPI documents so one Swagger UI lists every service.
Expose it only outside Production, or behind authentication.
Confirm one page lists all endpoints.

sections.name: Blazor Front-end (Patient & Doctor portals + DICOM Viewport)
sections.goal: A Blazor Web App delivering the Patient journey (register, book, view report, prescription, cart/checkout, follow-up) and the Doctor journey (studies list, viewport with lock indicator, write report), with a Cornerstone.js DICOM viewer.

tasks.title: Create Blazor Web App project
tasks.details: `dotnet new blazor` (interactive auto/server render modes) targeting .NET 10; configure the typed API client against the gateway.
acceptanceCriteria: App runs and calls a gateway endpoint
steps: Run `dotnet new blazor -n MediView.Web -o src/Web/MediView.Web --interactivity Server`.
Add it to the solution.
Create the folder structure: Features/Auth, Features/Studies, Features/Booking, Features/Billing, Features/Admin, Shared/.
Delete the sample Counter/Weather pages.
Create three layouts: PatientLayout, DoctorLayout, AdminLayout, chosen by role.
Add the IBM Plex fonts and a site.css with the design tokens (navy ink, teal accent, the four status colours).
Run it and confirm the shell renders.

tasks.title: Implement authentication in the UI
tasks.details: Handle login/refresh token storage, auth state provider, and protected routes/role-based UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Login persists session; protected pages gated
steps: Add Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization.
Create `JwtAuthenticationStateProvider : AuthenticationStateProvider` parsing claims from the access token.
Store tokens in a server-side session or a protected cookie - not in localStorage (XSS risk).
Wrap the app in CascadingAuthenticationState in Routes.razor.
Add a DelegatingHandler that attaches the bearer token and transparently refreshes on 401.
Add login/logout pages calling the Auth endpoints.
Test that a page marked [Authorize] redirects to login when signed out.

tasks.title: Build the Patient portal (booking, status, results, bill)
tasks.details: The Patient portal shows the patient's booking, the live Study status (todo / in-progress / re-diagnosis / done), the diagnosis result and prescription once ready, and the bill - which the patient pays from their wallet.
acceptanceCriteria: Patient can complete the end-to-end journey in the UI
steps: Create Features/Patient/Dashboard.razor listing the patient's studies with status pills.
Create Booking.razor, StudyDetail.razor (status, result, prescription) and Wallet.razor.
Bind status pills to the exact four labels: To do, In progress, Re-diagnosis, Done.
Show the result PDF link and prescription only when the report is finalized.
Show the bill with a Pay from wallet action and the resulting balance.
Test the whole patient journey against a seeded study.

tasks.title: Build the Doctor dashboard (booked studies within working hours)
tasks.details: The Doctor dashboard lists the patients booked within the doctor's working hours with each Study's status, opens the DICOM Viewport to diagnose, exports the result and prescription, and sets the Study status to re-diagnosis or done.
acceptanceCriteria: Doctor sees assigned Studies and can open one
steps: Create Features/Doctor/Worklist.razor calling GET /studies filtered to the doctor's own bookings.
Render columns: time, patient, MRN, study, modality, status, lock owner, action.
Add status filter chips and a count per status.
Disable Open and show the holder when a study is locked by someone else.
Wire the row action to navigate to the viewport.
Confirm only studies inside the doctor's working hours appear.

tasks.title: Integrate the DICOM Viewport with Cornerstone.js
tasks.details: Integrate the Cornerstone.js stack through Blazor JS interop: cornerstone-core, cornerstone-wado-image-loader with dicom-parser (loads DICOM from the Imaging service's WADO-RS endpoints) and cornerstone-tools for interactions. Build a Razor viewport component that hosts the canvas element and calls a JS module (IJSObjectReference) to display images, set window/level (VOI), zoom, pan, scroll through multi-frame stacks, and run measurement tools (length, angle, ROI).
acceptanceCriteria: A DICOM series renders in-browser with window/level, zoom, pan, and stack scrolling
steps: Add the Cornerstone libraries to wwwroot (or via npm + a bundler): cornerstone-core, cornerstone-wado-image-loader, dicom-parser, cornerstone-tools.
Write `wwwroot/js/viewport.js` as an ES module exporting init, loadStack, setWindowLevel, enableTool and dispose.
Configure the WADO image loader with the Imaging service base URL and the auth header.
In Viewport.razor, inject IJSRuntime and import the module with `InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", "./js/viewport.js")`.
Call init with the canvas element reference (ElementReference) in OnAfterRenderAsync.
Wire the toolbar: window/level, zoom, pan, stack scroll, length, angle, ROI.
Implement IAsyncDisposable and call module.dispose() then DisposeAsync so listeners never leak.
Test loading a real imported study.

tasks.title: Surface lock status + report editor
tasks.details: Show LOCKED indicator and owner; allow only the lock owner to edit/save the report from the viewport.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-owner viewport is read-only with clear lock UI
steps: Call GET /studies/{id}/lock on viewport open and render the banner from the response.
If you own the lock, show a countdown to expiry and an extend action.
If someone else owns it, render the read-only banner with their name and a Notify me when free button.
Disable every editing control when read-only - and rely on the API to enforce it too.
Build the report editor with Findings and Impression fields plus Save draft and Finalize.
On Finalize, ask for the decision (Done or Re-diagnosis) before submitting.

tasks.title: Real-time lock updates (SignalR, optional)
tasks.details: Push lock acquire/release updates to connected doctors via SignalR for instant UI feedback.
acceptanceCriteria: Lock changes reflect without manual refresh
steps: Add the Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client package.
Create a scoped `RealtimeService` owning one HubConnection for the whole shell.
Build the connection with the access token provider and WithAutomaticReconnect.
Register handlers for LockAcquired, LockExpiring, LockReleased, StudyStatusChanged and StudyImported.
Expose C# events the components subscribe to, and call StateHasChanged via InvokeAsync.
Join and leave the study group as the user navigates.
Test with two browsers side by side.

tasks.title: UI error handling + loading states
tasks.details: Consistent handling of ProblemDetails errors, 409 conflicts, and loading/empty states.
acceptanceCriteria: Errors and conflicts render friendly messages
steps: Add a global ErrorBoundary in the layout with a friendly fallback.
Create a shared LoadingSpinner and use skeletons on the worklist and study lists.
Map API ProblemDetails to toast messages, showing the owner name on a 409.
Disable submit buttons while a request is in flight to stop double-submits.
Add an empty state for every list.
Test with the API stopped to confirm nothing shows a raw exception.

tasks.title: Blazor hosting model and interop discipline
tasks.details: Use Blazor Server for the viewport (low latency, DICOM stays server-side). Keep components free of server-only types so a later WASM swap stays possible. Cornerstone runs through an IJSObjectReference module disposed in IAsyncDisposable; the SignalR client is a scoped service shared by the shell, not per-component.
acceptanceCriteria: Leaving the viewport disposes the JS module and leaks no listeners
steps: Confirm the project runs with Server interactivity for the viewport.
Keep server-only types out of components so a later WASM swap stays possible.
Audit every JS interop call for a matching dispose in IAsyncDisposable.
Make the SignalR connection a scoped service, not one per component.
Document the hosting decision and its rationale in docs/.

tasks.title: Typed API clients with resilience
tasks.details: One typed HttpClient per service registered with AddHttpClient plus Polly retry and circuit breaker. No component constructs an HttpClient.
acceptanceCriteria: Components depend on typed clients only
steps: Create one typed client interface per service (IStudyApi, IBookingApi, IBillingApi).
Register each with `builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IStudyApi, StudyApi>(c => c.BaseAddress = ...)`.
Attach the auth DelegatingHandler to each.
Add Polly: `.AddStandardResilienceHandler()` or explicit retry + circuit breaker + timeout.
Search the solution for `new HttpClient(` and remove every occurrence.
Test behaviour when a downstream service is down - the UI degrades, it does not hang.

tasks.title: Authorization-aware UI
tasks.details: CascadingAuthenticationState with AuthorizeView Policy="..." so the UI hides what the API would refuse. UI checks are convenience; the API remains the authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Hiding a control never becomes the only thing preventing an action
steps: Wrap role-specific navigation in `<AuthorizeView Policy="study.diagnose">`.
Hide the admin nav behind the admin policies.
Ensure the permission claims flow into the ClaimsPrincipal the provider builds.
Confirm every hidden action is ALSO refused by the API - test by calling it directly with curl.
Write in the code review checklist: UI checks are convenience, the API is the authority.

tasks.title: Screen: sign in / register (01)
tasks.details: Registration creates a Patient account only; sign-in serves all three roles and routes to the right shell.
acceptanceCriteria: Registering yields a Patient account and lands on the patient shell
steps: Build Login.razor with username and password and a link to register.
Build Register.razor collecting username, email, password and full name.
State on the form that registration creates a patient account.
After login, read the role claim and redirect to the patient, doctor or admin shell.
Show a clear error for wrong credentials and for a locked account.
Test all three roles land on the right shell.

tasks.title: Screens: patient booking and follow-up (02, 13)
tasks.details: Booking shows only slots inside the chosen doctor's working hours. Follow-up booking is prefilled from the prior study, defaults to the same doctor, and links the new study to the old one via parent_study_id.
acceptanceCriteria: A follow-up booking creates a study linked to its parent
steps: Build Booking.razor: pick a doctor, pick a date, then load slots from GET /doctors/{id}/slots.
Render only returned slots - never generate times on the client.
Show a clear message when the doctor has no hours that day.
Build FollowUpBooking.razor opened from a finished study, prefilled with the prior study, doctor and modality.
Display 'Follows Study NNN' and pass parentStudyId on submit.
Test that the created study carries ParentStudyId.

tasks.title: Screens: patient status, results and wallet (03, 04, 12)
tasks.details: Status page uses the same four labels the doctor sees. Results show the report PDF and issued prescription. Wallet pays the diagnosis-fee bill; the cart checks out the medication order separately.
acceptanceCriteria: The patient sees live status and can pay both bill kinds
steps: Build the study status page using the same four labels and colours as the doctor's view.
Show the result PDF and issued prescription once finalized, plus a follow-up prompt when follow_up_weeks is set.
Build Wallet.razor showing the balance, the unpaid diagnosis-fee bill and a Pay action.
Build Cart.razor from the issued prescription with quantities locked and only remove allowed.
Show the projected balance after payment before the patient confirms.
Test paying both bill kinds.

tasks.title: Screens: doctor worklist and viewport (05, 06, 07)
tasks.details: The worklist lists studies booked in the doctor's hours with status and lock owner. Opening a study takes the lock and moves it to In progress. A study locked elsewhere renders read-only with the owner, lock age, auto-release countdown and a "Notify me when free" action.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a free study takes the lock; a locked one is read-only with owner and countdown
steps: Wire the worklist row action to open the viewport, which calls POST /studies/{id}/lock.
On success, confirm the status moved to In progress and start the heartbeat timer.
On 409, open in read-only mode showing the owner, lock age and countdown.
Add the Notify me when free button calling POST /studies/{id}/watch.
Handle LockReleased by offering to take over without a page reload.
Test the three states: free, held by me, held by another.

tasks.title: Screen: prescription composer (11)
tasks.details: Opens over the viewport while the doctor holds the lock, searches the formulary, warns on allergies, and attaches to the report so it is issued on finalize.
acceptanceCriteria: A composed prescription is issued exactly when the report is finalized
steps: Build PrescriptionComposer.razor as a panel over the viewport.
Add drug search hitting GET /drugs?q= with debounce.
On add, call the allergy check and show a prominent warning the doctor must confirm.
List added items with dosage, frequency, duration, quantity and the running patient cost.
Save as a draft attached to the report; do not issue here.
Confirm issuing happens only when the report is finalized.
Test with an allergic patient.

tasks.title: Screens: admin onboarding, import, audit, roles, flags (08, 09, 10, 14)
tasks.details: Doctor onboarding with credential upload and verification; x-ray import simulation showing staged instances and the target study; audit log with actor, reason and before/after; the roles matrix with server-enforced cells greyed out and study.diagnose never grantable to Admin.
acceptanceCriteria: An admin can onboard a doctor, import a study, review the audit trail, and cannot grant themselves diagnose
steps: Build DoctorOnboarding.razor: create the account, upload credential files, then a Verify action.
Build Import.razor: file picker, staged instance list with size and count, target study, and an explicit To do -> To do note.
Build AuditLog.razor with filters by actor, entity and date, showing reason and a before/after diff.
Build RolesMatrix.razor rendering permissions x roles, with non-grantable cells greyed and disabled.
Build FeatureFlags.razor listing flags read-only with their internal/external state.
Confirm the UI cannot grant study.diagnose to Admin, and that the API refuses it too.

tasks.title: Screen: patient mobile (15)
tasks.details: Responsive fall-back for the patient side only; doctor and admin remain desktop-only.
acceptanceCriteria: The patient journey is usable at mobile width
steps: Add responsive CSS breakpoints for the patient layout only.
Collapse the patient nav into a bottom tab bar under ~600px.
Stack cards vertically and enlarge tap targets to at least 44px.
Leave the doctor and admin shells desktop-only with a clear message on small screens.
Test the full patient journey at 390px width.

tasks.title: Render performance on long lists
tasks.details: @key on list items, ShouldRender on the viewport, and virtualization on the worklist and audit log.
acceptanceCriteria: The worklist stays responsive with hundreds of studies
steps: Add `@key` to every list item bound to an id.
Add `<Virtualize>` to the worklist and audit log.
Override ShouldRender on the viewport so unrelated state changes do not re-render the canvas.
Debounce SignalR-driven refreshes.
Load-test with several hundred studies and confirm the list stays responsive.

sections.name: Cross-cutting: Messaging, Observability & Resilience
sections.goal: Shared async messaging (MassTransit + Outbox), structured logging (Serilog), distributed tracing/metrics (OpenTelemetry), health checks, and resilience (Polly) across all services.

tasks.title: Set up MassTransit with RabbitMQ
tasks.details: Add a shared messaging extension configuring MassTransit over RabbitMQ locally (Azure Service Bus in prod) with consumer registration.
acceptanceCriteria: A test message publishes and is consumed
steps: Add MassTransit and MassTransit.RabbitMQ to each service's Infrastructure.
Configure `AddMassTransit(x => { x.AddConsumers(assembly); x.UsingRabbitMq((ctx,cfg) => { cfg.Host(...); cfg.ConfigureEndpoints(ctx); }); })`.
Set a kebab-case endpoint name formatter so queue names are predictable.
Reference MediView.Contracts for the message types.
Publish one test event and confirm it appears in the RabbitMQ management UI.

tasks.title: Implement the Transactional Outbox
tasks.details: Enable MassTransit EF Core Outbox so events publish atomically with the local DB transaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Events are not lost on partial failures
steps: Add MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCore.
In AddMassTransit, add `x.AddEntityFrameworkOutbox<TDbContext>(o => { o.UsePostgres(); o.UseBusOutbox(); })`.
Add the outbox tables to the service's migration.
Change publishing code to use IPublishEndpoint inside the same DbContext transaction as the domain change.
Confirm the message row lands in the outbox table before the bus receives it.
Test the crash case: throw after SaveChanges and confirm the message still relays on restart.

tasks.title: Add Serilog structured logging
tasks.details: Configure Serilog with enrichers (correlation id, service name) and sinks to console + Seq locally.
acceptanceCriteria: Logs are structured and visible in Seq
steps: Add Serilog.AspNetCore and the Seq (or console JSON) sink.
Configure Serilog in Program.cs before anything else so startup errors are captured.
Enrich with ServiceName, Environment, MachineName and CorrelationId.
Add `app.UseSerilogRequestLogging()`.
Convert every log call to structured form with named placeholders.
Grep the codebase for logs containing patient names or report text and remove them.

tasks.title: Add OpenTelemetry tracing + metrics
tasks.details: Instrument ASP.NET Core, HttpClient, EF Core, Redis, and MassTransit; export traces/metrics (OTLP) and propagate context across the bus.
acceptanceCriteria: A request trace spans gateway->service->bus
steps: Add OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting plus the ASP.NET Core, HttpClient, EF Core and MassTransit instrumentation packages.
Configure tracing and metrics with the OTLP exporter pointing at the local collector.
Set the service name per service so traces are attributable.
Add custom spans around lock acquisition and DICOM import.
Confirm one request produces a single trace spanning gateway -> service -> bus.

tasks.title: Add health checks everywhere
tasks.details: Add liveness/readiness checks (DB, Redis, broker, downstream) to every service and the gateway.
acceptanceCriteria: /health/ready reflects real dependency health
steps: Add AddHealthChecks to every service with checks for Npgsql, Redis and RabbitMQ.
Map /health/live (process is up) and /health/ready (dependencies are reachable) separately.
Tag dependency checks as 'ready' so liveness never fails on a transient dependency blip.
Wire the endpoints into docker-compose healthchecks.
Test by stopping Redis and confirming ready fails while live still passes.

tasks.title: Apply Polly resilience policies
tasks.details: Add retry, timeout, and circuit-breaker policies to HttpClient calls and message consumers.
acceptanceCriteria: Transient failures retry; breakers open under sustained failure
steps: Add Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience (or Polly directly).
Add `.AddStandardResilienceHandler()` to every typed HttpClient.
Tune: 3 retries with exponential backoff and jitter, a circuit breaker, and a per-attempt timeout.
Never retry non-idempotent POSTs without an idempotency key.
Add a fallback so a failing non-critical dependency degrades rather than fails the request.
Test by pausing a downstream container.

tasks.title: Pluggable provider abstraction (feature-flagged: internal now, external later)
tasks.details: Put Auth, DICOM import, and Payment behind provider interfaces (IAuthProvider, IDicomImportProvider, IPaymentProvider), each with two implementations - an internal build-from-scratch one and an external third-party one - selected per provider by a config flag (false = internal, true = external). Default every flag to internal so the system runs end-to-end with no external dependencies now, and can switch to a real IdP / PACS / payment gateway later without touching callers.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth, DICOM import, and Payment each resolve to an internal or external provider by config flag; internal is the default
steps: Create `IAuthProvider`, `IDicomImportProvider` and `IPaymentProvider` in Application.
Write the internal implementation for each (JWT, own DICOM code, wallet).
Write an external stub for each that throws NotImplementedException for now.
Create `FeatureFlagOptions` bound from configuration with three booleans defaulting to false.
Register with a factory choosing the implementation by flag at startup.
Confirm callers depend only on the interface, never on the concrete type.
Flip a flag in config and confirm the resolved implementation changes.

tasks.title: gRPC for synchronous cross-service queries
tasks.details: Commands that need an answer now go over gRPC (e.g. Booking asking Identity for doctor availability). Put .proto files in MediView.Contracts, version them, and never repurpose a field number.
acceptanceCriteria: Services query each other over typed gRPC contracts, not ad-hoc HTTP
steps: Add Grpc.AspNetCore to the serving projects and Grpc.Net.ClientFactory to callers.
Put .proto files in MediView.Contracts under Protos/ with `<Protobuf Include="..." />` items.
Define the services you actually need: GetDoctorAvailability, GetPatientAllergies, GetLockStatus.
Implement the server side in the owning service's Api project and map with MapGrpcService.
Register clients with AddGrpcClient and attach resilience.
Version by adding new fields with new numbers - never reuse or repurpose a field number.
Test one cross-service call end to end.

tasks.title: Transactional outbox and idempotent consumers
tasks.details: Use the MassTransit EF outbox so the domain change and the event publish commit in the same transaction, then relay. Consumers dedupe on MessageId: delivery is at-least-once, never exactly-once.
acceptanceCriteria: A crash between save and publish loses no event; redelivery causes no double effect
steps: Confirm the outbox is enabled in every publishing service.
Add an InboxMessage table (or use MassTransit's) recording processed message ids.
At the top of each consumer, check whether the message id was already processed and return early if so.
Make the effect itself idempotent as a second line of defence (upsert, not insert).
Test by manually redelivering a message and asserting no double effect.

tasks.title: Local read replicas for cross-service joins
tasks.details: You cannot JOIN across services. On hot paths (the worklist), keep a small local projection - e.g. a doctor directory in the Patient service updated from DoctorVerified events - and join locally. Queries replicate; commands call.
acceptanceCriteria: The worklist renders without a synchronous call to another service
steps: Identify the hot-path joins that would need another service - start with the worklist's doctor name.
Create a small local table, e.g. patient.doctor_directory (doctor_id, full_name, department, is_verified).
Add a consumer for DoctorVerified/DoctorUpdated that upserts into it.
Rewrite the worklist query to join locally.
Accept the eventual consistency and document the staleness window.
Backfill the replica once at startup for existing data.

tasks.title: Retries, backoff and a monitored dead-letter queue
tasks.details: Exponential backoff with jitter on consumers, then a dead-letter queue that is actually alerted on and has a documented replay procedure.
acceptanceCriteria: Poison messages land in the DLQ and raise an alert
steps: Configure `cfg.UseMessageRetry(r => r.Exponential(3, 1s, 30s, 5s))` on the bus.
Add jitter so retries from many consumers do not synchronise.
Confirm failed messages land in the _error queue.
Add an alert when the error queue depth exceeds zero for more than N minutes.
Write a documented replay procedure (shovel from _error back to the queue).
Test by throwing in a consumer and watching the message reach the error queue.

tasks.title: Correlation ids and structured logging
tasks.details: CorrelationIdMiddleware accepts or creates X-Correlation-Id, pushes it into the Serilog scope, and propagates it over HTTP, gRPC and the bus. Log structurally (never interpolated) and NEVER log PHI - no patient name, DOB or report text; log ids only.
acceptanceCriteria: One request is traceable across gateway, services and bus, and logs contain no PHI
steps: Create `CorrelationIdMiddleware` reading X-Correlation-Id or creating a new Guid.
Push it into the Serilog LogContext for the request scope and echo it in the response header.
Add a DelegatingHandler forwarding it on outgoing HTTP calls.
Add a MassTransit filter putting it on message headers and restoring it in consumers.
Include it on audit rows.
Trace one request across the gateway, two services and the bus using only the id.
Re-audit logs for PHI one final time.

tasks.title: Typed, validated configuration
tasks.details: Bind settings to typed options with ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart() so a bad environment variable fails at boot, not at runtime. Precedence: appsettings -> environment -> Key Vault. No secrets in the repository; user-secrets locally.
acceptanceCriteria: A missing or malformed setting stops the service at startup with a clear message
steps: Create an options class per settings section: JwtOptions, RedisOptions, FeatureFlagOptions, BillingOptions.
Annotate required properties with [Required] and ranges where sensible.
Bind with `.Bind(section).ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart()`.
Inject IOptions<T> (or IOptionsMonitor for values that can change).
Remove every direct IConfiguration["key"] read from handlers.
Test by deleting a required setting and confirming startup fails with a clear message.

tasks.title: DI registration and lifetime discipline
tasks.details: Each layer exposes AddApplication()/AddInfrastructure(config) so Program.cs reads as a table of contents. DbContext, repositories and handlers are scoped; stateless helpers and IConnectionMultiplexer are singletons; a scoped service is never injected into a singleton (use IServiceScopeFactory in workers).
acceptanceCriteria: No captive-dependency warnings and Program.cs contains no per-type registrations
steps: Give each layer a DependencyInjection.cs with AddApplication() / AddInfrastructure(config).
Move every per-type registration out of Program.cs into those methods.
Register DbContext, repositories and handlers as scoped; IConnectionMultiplexer and stateless helpers as singletons.
Find any singleton depending on a scoped service and fix it with IServiceScopeFactory.
Enable scope validation: `builder.Host.UseDefaultServiceProvider(o => { o.ValidateScopes = true; o.ValidateOnBuild = true; })`.
Run every service and confirm no captive-dependency errors at startup.

sections.name: Security & Compliance
sections.goal: Health-data-grade security: TLS everywhere, secrets in Key Vault, encryption at rest, PII protection, audit logging, least-privilege identities, and GDPR/HIPAA-minded data handling.

tasks.title: Enforce HTTPS/TLS and security headers
tasks.details: Require HTTPS, enable HSTS, and add security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) at the gateway and services.
acceptanceCriteria: Traffic is TLS-only with hardened headers
steps: Add `app.UseHttpsRedirection()` and HSTS outside Development.
Add security headers: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy, and a Content-Security-Policy.
Allow the WADO origin and blob host in the CSP so Cornerstone can load images.
Disable the server header.
Scan the deployed site with a headers checker and fix what it flags.

tasks.title: Centralize secrets in Key Vault
tasks.details: Move connection strings/keys to Azure Key Vault referenced via managed identity; remove secrets from config/repo.
acceptanceCriteria: No secrets in code; services read from Key Vault
steps: Create the Key Vault (Bicep) and add Azure.Identity + the Key Vault configuration provider.
Add secrets: database connection strings, JWT signing key, storage keys.
Chain the provider in Program.cs when running outside Development.
Authenticate with a user-assigned managed identity - no client secrets in config.
Confirm no secret literal remains in any appsettings file.

tasks.title: Encrypt data at rest + protect PII
tasks.details: Enable DB/Blob encryption at rest and add field-level encryption/hashing for sensitive PII where needed.
acceptanceCriteria: Sensitive fields encrypted; storage encrypted at rest
steps: Enable encryption at rest on Postgres and Blob (default on Azure - confirm it).
Enforce TLS on the database connection (`SSL Mode=Require`).
Confirm DICOM de-identification runs on import, so stored pixel metadata carries the anonymous name.
Restrict PII columns to the services that own them.
Document what counts as PHI in this system.

tasks.title: Implement access audit logging
tasks.details: Log who accessed/modified which Study/report (immutable audit trail) for compliance investigations. Maps to audit.audit_log with actor_user_id, actor_role, action, entity_type/entity_id, reason, before_data/after_data jsonb and ip_address.
acceptanceCriteria: Study access/edits produce audit entries
steps: Create the AuditLog entity and DbContext in the audit schema.
Create `IAuditWriter` in Application with a Write method taking actor, action, entity, reason and before/after.
Serialize before/after to jsonb, redacting fields you must not store.
Call it from every override, force-release, role grant and import.
Add indexes on (entity_type, entity_id, created_at) and (actor_user_id, created_at).
Add GET /admin/audit with filters for the audit screen.

tasks.title: Least-privilege identities and RBAC
tasks.details: Use managed identities and scoped RBAC so each service has only the Azure permissions it needs.
acceptanceCriteria: Each service uses a scoped managed identity
steps: Create one user-assigned managed identity per service.
Grant each only what it needs: this service's Key Vault secrets, its own blob container, its own database role.
Create per-service Postgres roles with access to their own schema only.
Remove any shared superuser connection string.
Verify by attempting a cross-schema query with a service's own credentials - it must fail.

tasks.title: GDPR/HIPAA data-handling controls
tasks.details: Add data-retention policy and a right-to-erasure workflow; document data-processing and lawful basis.
acceptanceCriteria: Retention + erasure workflow documented and testable
steps: Write docs/compliance.md listing PHI fields and where they live.
Define retention: how long studies, reports and audit rows are kept.
Implement an export endpoint (data subject access) returning a patient's own data.
Define the deletion policy: soft-delete clinical records, and document why hard deletion is refused.
Add consent capture at registration if you want the full flow.
Note that this is a student project, not a certified system, and say so in the UI footer.

tasks.title: Dependency and container scanning
tasks.details: Enable dependency vulnerability scanning and image scanning in CI (see S19).
acceptanceCriteria: Vulnerable dependencies/images flagged in CI
steps: Add `dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive` to CI and fail on any hit.
Add Trivy (or Microsoft Defender) image scanning after the container build.
Enable Dependabot or Renovate for package updates.
Pin base images by digest, not just tag.
Fix or document every High/Critical finding before deploying.

tasks.title: PHI access logging (who read the record)
tasks.details: Write audit.access_log for every PHI read - view_study, view_report, view_images, export_pdf - with actor, role, patient, study and IP. Healthcare systems must answer who LOOKED at a record, not only who changed it.
acceptanceCriteria: Every patient-data read is attributable to a user and timestamp
steps: Create the AccessLog entity: ActorUserId, ActorRole, PatientId, StudyId, Action, IpAddress.
Create `AccessLogMiddleware` (or an action filter) that fires on PHI read endpoints.
Log actions: view_study, view_report, view_images, export_pdf.
Keep it asynchronous (a channel + background writer) so it never slows the request.
Add an index on (patient_id, created_at).
Add an admin query answering 'who viewed this patient's records'.
Test that opening a study writes exactly one access row.

tasks.title: Soft-delete clinical records
tasks.details: Nothing in a patient's clinical history is hard-deleted. Use soft deletion with EF global query filters; corrections to finalized reports are addenda.
acceptanceCriteria: No endpoint hard-deletes a study, report, or prescription
steps: Add an IsDeleted flag (and DeletedAt/DeletedBy) to clinical entities.
Add EF global query filters: `builder.HasQueryFilter(x => !x.IsDeleted)`.
Replace every Remove call on clinical data with a soft delete.
Add IgnoreQueryFilters to the admin/audit views that must see everything.
Confirm no endpoint issues a hard DELETE on studies, reports or prescriptions.

tasks.title: Feature flags as first-class configuration
tasks.details: Model config.feature_flags (auth.provider.external, dicom.import.external, payment.provider.external), default every flag to internal, surface them read-only on the admin screen, and audit every change.
acceptanceCriteria: Flags default to internal and every change is audited
steps: Create the FeatureFlag entity in the config schema and seed the three flags as disabled (internal).
Load them at startup and cache them, refreshing periodically.
Add GET /admin/flags returning them for the admin screen.
Make changes admin-only and write an audit row for every toggle.
Keep the screen read-only for now if you do not want runtime switching yet.
Confirm the default path uses internal providers with no external calls.

sections.name: CI/CD Pipeline
sections.goal: Automated build and gated deployment: build and analyze on every PR, containerize each service, scan and push images to ACR, run EF migrations, and deploy to Azure with environment approvals.

tasks.title: Build and analyze on every pull request
tasks.details: GitHub Actions workflow: restore, build in Release, and run Roslyn analyzers plus `dotnet format` verification on every PR.
acceptanceCriteria: PRs are blocked unless the build and analyzers pass
steps: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml triggered on pull_request and push to main.
Add steps: checkout, setup-dotnet with 10.x, `dotnet restore`, `dotnet build -c Release --no-restore`.
Add `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to enforce style.
Add the architecture-rule check so a Domain layering violation fails here.
Add `dotnet list package --vulnerable` and fail on findings.
Enable branch protection requiring this workflow to pass.

tasks.title: Containerize each service
tasks.details: Add multi-stage Dockerfiles (or `dotnet publish` container build) for every service, the gateway, and the Blazor app.
acceptanceCriteria: Each service produces a runnable image locally
steps: Write a multi-stage Dockerfile per service under build/.
Stage 1: the SDK image, copy csproj files first, restore, then copy the rest and publish - so restore layers cache.
Stage 2: the aspnet:10.0 runtime image, copy the publish output, set a non-root USER, EXPOSE the port.
Add a HEALTHCHECK hitting /health/live.
Add .dockerignore excluding bin, obj and .git.
Build and run one image locally to confirm it serves traffic.

tasks.title: Scan and push images to ACR
tasks.details: Scan images (e.g., Trivy), then push tagged images to Azure Container Registry on main.
acceptanceCriteria: Scanned images published to ACR on main
steps: Create the ACR in Bicep and grant the CI identity AcrPush.
Add a workflow job that logs in with `azure/login` and builds each image.
Tag with both the git SHA and latest.
Run the Trivy scan and fail on High/Critical.
Push only on main, never from a pull request.
Verify the tags appear in the registry.

tasks.title: Automate EF Core migrations
